There are many interesting challenges ahead, and we're happy for people to move between teams or to specialise, whatever you prefer. title: Senior Backend Engineer
description: <div class="content-intro"><p><strong><em>🚀 We’re on a mission to make money work for everyone.</em></strong></p> <p>We’re waving goodbye to the complicated and confusing ways of traditional banking.</p> <p>After starting as a prepaid card, our product offering has grown a lot in the last 10 years in the UK. As well as <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/personal">personal</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/business-banking">business</a> bank accounts, we offer <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/joint-account">joint accounts</a>, <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/16-17">accounts for 16-17 year olds</a>, a <a href="https://monzo.com/current-account/under-16s">free kids account</a> and <a href="https://monzo.com/flex">credit cards</a> in the UK, with more exciting things to come beyond. We have big ambitions for the future, and technology plays a big role in creating a bank our customers want, so engineers at Monzo collaborate across disciplines to solve interesting challenges throughout the company.</p> <p>These range from the products our customers use everyday to underlying infrastructure, security, payments and finance, customer operations, financial crime, and data, to name just a few areas. As a bank, there is scope for impact across a huge number of opportunities.</p> <p>We contribute to <a href="https://github.com/monzo"><strong>open source software</strong></a> as much as possible. Our <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/technology"><strong>blog</strong></a><strong> </strong>is a good place to learn even more about what we do!</p> <p><strong>Your day-to-day   </strong></p> <p>This role is all about collaborating with your team to make a difference to your customers. As a backend engineer you’ll work in a squad alongside other disciplines like product managers, marketers, user researchers, designers, mobile engineers, web engineers, data analysts, business analysts, writers and more! </p> <p>Together you'll build and support a particular part of Monzo. Our squads belong to our wider collectives (a word we use to describe self-governing business units of ~100 people). They are: Core Banking, Business Banking, Wealth, Borrowing, Growth, Payments, Platform, Fincrime, Security & Expansion. All of our collectives are doing innovative work, many of which have machine learning and AI at the forefront- from fighting financial crime to building smarter financial tools - and you may have the opportunity to join a collective that gives you direct exposure to this exciting space.</p> <p>They’re all looking for additional Backend Engineers right now, we do a standard interview process across all our collectives and at the end we will find the best match for you based on your skills, experience, preferences and aligning with the business need! </p> <p>Our backend engineers have a variety of different backgrounds. As long as you enjoy learning new things, we’d love to talk to you. We do not ask for formal qualifications or degree requirements for any of our engineering roles.</p> <p><strong>How we work 💻</strong></p> <p>Our main tech hub is in London, but our engineers live everywhere in the UK— from Brighton to the Western Isles. We value meeting in person but we don't have a mandated requirement on office attendance, even if you're nearby. We believe you'll do your best work if you are where you want to be. If you live outside of London and we ask you to come into the office, Monzo will support you with the costs ✨</p> <p>Our offices are naturally social, especially Tuesdays, Wednesdays and Thursdays, which happen to line up with our twice-weekly Monzo lunches & treat Thursdays 🍽️</p> <p>Teams also schedule time together often for work and play – in or around the office, or online.</p> <p><strong>Set up a work schedule that delivers impact and fits your life:</strong></p> <p>At Monzo, we value connections, flexibility, and wellbeing. We keep our meetings during core hours to stay connected and believe in maintaining work/life balance.</p> <p>You’ll be empowered to manage your work in a way that suits you and your team, giving you the freedom for children drop-offs and pick-ups, walking your dog or adventurous cat, avoiding peak commuting times or gym slots, appointments, or supporting your family in an emergency 🕣✨</p> <p>If you prefer to work part-time, we'll make this happen whenever we can - whether this is to help you meet other commitments or strike a great work-life balance.</p> <p><strong>Work the way that works for you with Monzo! 💼</strong></p> <p><strong>You should apply if:</strong></p> <ul> <li>you have strong experience working on the backend of a technology product</li> <li>you want to be involved in building a product that you (and the people you know) use every day</li> <li>you have a product mindset: you care about customer outcomes and you want to make data-informed decisions</li> <li>you’re comfortable working in a team that deals with ambiguity</li> <li>you’re interested in distributed systems and writing resilient software</li> <li>you have some experience with strongly-typed languages (Go, Java, C, Scala etc.).</li> <li>you think you’d enjoy the kind of work we’re doing</li> </ul> <p>We're on the look out for L50 Engineers at the moment, you can read more in our <a href="https://monzo.com/documents/engineering-progression-framework-v4-1.pdf">Engineering Progression Framework </a>- we will interview you across the whole frame work, so if you are not sure what level you are aiming for please chat to your recruiters! </p> <p><em>Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! Studies show that women and people of colour might hesitate to apply unless they meet every single requirement. At Monzo, we’re dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming team. If you’re passionate about this role and keen to learn and grow with us, we encourage you to apply— even if you don’t have everything thats listed just yet. Drop us your application, we’d love to hear from you!</em></p> <p><strong>What you’ll be working on: </strong></p> <p>We hire very technically agnostic so whilst we use the below technologies we do not expect prior knowledge, you will be fully supported in our organised onboarding to get up to speed in the below: </p> <ul> <li><a href="http://golang.org/"><strong>Go</strong></a> to write our application code (there’s an excellent interactive Go tutorial <a href="https://tour.golang.org/welcome/1"><strong>here</strong></a>)</li> <li><a href="http://cassandra.apache.org/"><strong>Cassandra</strong></a> for most persistent data storage</li> <li><a href="http://kafka.apache.org/"><strong>Kafka</strong></a> for our asynchronous message queue</li> <li><a href="http://kubernetes.io/"><strong>Kubernetes</strong></a> and <a href="https://www.docker.com/"><strong>Docker</strong></a> to schedule and run our services </li> <li><a href="https://www.envoyproxy.io/"><strong>Envoy Proxy</strong></a> for RPC</li> <li><a href="http://aws.amazon.com/"><strong>AWS</strong></a> for most of our production infrastructure and<a actual cables to connect to various third parties</li> </ul> <p><strong>The Interview Process:</strong></p> <p>Our interview process involves three main stages: </p> <ol> <li>Initial Call </li> <li>Take home task or pair coding exercise </li> <li>Final interview: including a system design and a behavioural interview </li> </ol> <p>Our average process takes around 4 weeks but we will always work around your availability. </p> <p>One of our engineers has written a detailed blog on their experience through this process, for extra details, hints and tips please see <a href="https://monzo.com/blog/2022/03/23/demystifying-the-backend-engineering-interview-process"><strong>here</strong></a>.</p> <p><strong>What’s in it for you:</strong></p> <p>💰 £105,000 - £135,000 + Incentive Awards tied to your performance</p> <p>✈️We can help you relocate to the UK </p> <p>✅We can sponsor visas.</p> <p>📍This role can be based in our London office, but we're open to distributed working within the UK (with ad hoc meetings in London).</p> <p>⏰We offer flexible working hours and trust you to work enough hours to do your job well, at times that suit you and your team.</p> <p>📚Learning budget of £1,000 a year for books, training courses and conferences</p> <p>➕And much more, see our full list of benefits <a href="https://monzo.com/careers/"><strong>here </strong></a></p> <p> </p> <p><em>We're usually always hiring for Backend Engineers, so there's no closing date for this job.</em></p> <p>#LI-Remote</p> <p>#LI-NB</p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p><strong>Equal opportunities for everyone</strong></p> <p>Diversity and inclusion are a priority for us and we’re making sure we have lots of title: Account Executive
description: <p><strong>Role: </strong>Account Executive</p> <p><strong>Location: </strong>United Kingdom</p> <p><strong><span style="color: rgb(224, 62, 45);">We Are</span>: </strong></p> <p>RTB House is a next-generation performance demand-side platform (DSP) that uses proprietary Deep Learning AI algorithms to help brands grow. The company is the market leader in driving performance using Deep Learning across the entire purchase funnel.</p> <p>Founded in 2012 and now operating in 90+ markets, RTB House has always been private-by-design. It embraces first-party advertising and a relentless approach to innovation. title: Social Media Content Creator
description: Getting homes off fossil fuels means fitting millions of heat pumps, solar panels and batteries, and every one has to be designed, sold and fitted by an installer. The assets themselves already work brilliantly, but getting them into homes is still slow, complex and painful. Our mission is to change that: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run a renewables installation business, and get homes off fossil fuels way faster. In just a few years we've become the leading platform for heat pump installers in the UK and Ireland, with around half of all heat pump installations now being managed on Spruce. We've just launched our solar and battery product, and we're building on that to go after even bigger opportunities: every other type of job these installers do, the rest of how they run their business, and a bunch of new countries. We're now on the hunt for someone truly brilliant to own our socials: making content installers look forward to watching, and turning that attention into customers. 🌲 About Spruce Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating. We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates. We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have doubled the team and grown revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, have just launched an end-to-end solar and battery product, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed… 🥖 The role You'll work closely with Hector and the wider growth team. You'll be our first dedicated social hire. Almost nobody is making great content for installers, so the field is wide open and it's yours to build. Your goal is to make Spruce the account every installer follows. Day-to-day you'll be: Making the content yourself – You'll take each piece from idea to script, shoot, edit and post: installer stories, site visits, founder clips, and new out-of-the-box ideas with a real shot at going viral. You'll have the freedom to try anything, and to bring in freelance editors or videographers when that gets better content out sooner. Getting people on camera – You'll spend time on site with our customers and make installers look brilliant on camera. You'll get our own team on camera too, from sales to the devs who build the product. Getting the mix right – You'll balance videos that entertain (skits, challenges, series), teach installers something useful, build trust through real installer stories, and show what Spruce does, so the account never feels like an advert. You'll keep testing new formats, trends and collabs with installer creators. Owning our socials – You'll run Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn and Facebook: the voice, what we make, and what goes out and when. You'll do more of what works and drop what doesn't. Building a community – You'll reply to comments and DMs yourself, and build a community of installers who want to be featured: an audience that becomes our customers. 🫵 About you We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft. You don't need a particular job title or a set number of years, but you do need to show us something you grew: an account, a channel, a series or a brand. You'll ideally be: A proven creator – you've grown an account, you've had videos that travelled well beyond your normal reach, and you can tell us why they worked; Obsessed with what works – you study what's working on TikTok, Reels and Shorts this week (not last year), you have strong opinions about hooks, and you're always learning what's taking off and what's dying; Properly hands-on – you do most of the shooting and editing yourself and you're quick, and you use AI tools to go faster; Comfortable on camera – you're happy being the talking head yourself, and even happier getting a great take out of an installer who's never been filmed; Curious about the numbers – you check how every post did because you want the next one to be better, not because you love a dashboard; Interested in installers – you see small business owners doing technically complex, physically demanding work, with a brilliant story in every one, and you want to understand their world, not just film it. Bonus points if you've had videos pass a million views or grown an account to 100k+ followers. … and you'll hopefully also love heat pumps! 🤓 🌟 Our offer 💰 £40–60k salary, depending on experience 🍰 Equity (options) in the company 🏡 Hybrid working: 2–3 days in-person a week (London or Bristol), with full-team meetups every fortnight 🏖️ 33 days holiday (25 plus bank holidays) and opportunity to work from abroad for another 30 days each year 🏥 Private Medical Cover (Vitality) 👧 Workplace Nursery Benefit scheme ( YellowNest ) 🧑‍🍼 Enhanced Parental Leave 🚲 Cycle to Work scheme 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Brilliant team to learn from and massive opportunity to grow 🧑‍💻 Working at Spruce We're currently a close-knit team of 35, split between London and Bristol. We spend 2–3 days each week working together in-person in both locations, and get everyone together every fortnight. You'll have genuine influence from day one. The best idea wins regardless of seniority. We expect you to challenge everything, ask "why?" multiple levels deep, and push back when something doesn't make sense. We want everyone to spend time with installers on-site, feel their pain points, then rapidly suggest and implement solutions based on real feedback rather than assumptions. We move fast and ship imperfect things, learning from users rather than trying to perfect in isolation. When things break, we focus on how we fix it and what we can learn – and never blame. You'll own your outcomes whilst knowing the team has your back. Feedback is constant, direct, and kind – we'll tell you when something isn't working and expect the same honesty (and empathy) back.Getting homes off fossil fuels means fitting millions of heat pumps, solar panels and batteries, and every one has to be designed, sold and fitted by an installer. The assets themselves already work brilliantly, but getting them into homes is still slow, complex and painful. Our mission is to change that: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run a renewables installation business, and get homes off fossil fuels way faster. Every enterprise is investing heavily in AI, but few are confident it will improve performance. Too often it goes to what’s easy to automate, disconnected from the decisions that actually move the business. Frontier works backwards from objectives like revenue, margin and risk to the decisions that drive them, then connects the data, models and agents those decisions need into a world model of the business. Teams simulate and optimise options with ADA, our AI decision agent, and every decision is tracked against its outcome so the system keeps learning. Our ambition is to make business decisions as easy to navigate as getting around a city. We don’t believe in AI that thinks for people. We believe in AI that helps people think, with humans and agents working together inside a decision system. Customers start with one high-value decision and prove value in weeks. Building trusted, multi-level relationships across accounts—engaging senior sponsors, business owners, and end users while acting as a customer advocate within Faculty. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. title: Group Data Protection Officer
description: Group Data Protection Officer | M-KOPA Remote (covering Kenya, Uganda, Nigeria, Ghana, South Africa and the UK) You're the lawyer people call when a data question has no easy answer. You're accomplished. You're respected. You're probably even happy. But is your work protecting millions of people who are trusting a formal financial service with their personal information for the very first time? That is the question at the heart of this role. The trust you'd be protecting M-KOPA now serves 10 million customers , up from 5 million in 2024, and has unlocked $2+ billion in credit . 86% of our customers report an improved quality of life, 70% use our products to earn an income, and 55% are accessing products and services for the first time. Behind them stand 2,300+ employees and 35,000 agents . Every one of those customers has handed us personal information, and they did it because they believed we would handle it with care. Across Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, South Africa, Uganda and the UK, that belief is held under six different sets of rules, each with its own expectations about consent, retention, cross-border transfers and what happens when something goes wrong. The customers who benefit most from what we build are often the ones with the least room to absorb a mistake with their data, and that is the standard this role exists to hold. Why this timing matters You may have seen us advertising several roles across Legal, Risk and Compliance. That is deliberate, not random. We've moved from 5 million customers to 7 million, and we are now building beyond 10 million. The legal, risk and privacy foundations have to be laid ahead of that growth, not scrambled together after it. New markets, new products and new partners all arrive with new data questions. Joining now means shaping the privacy programme while its biggest chapters are still ahead of it. What makes this different In many organisations, the data protection officer reviews things at the end of the process. Here, the role reaches the whole group. Your current role: one jurisdiction, one regime. This role: six markets, one customer promise. You would report day to day to the Chief Legal, Risk and Compliance Officer, with reporting to the CEO and the Board as well. Your recommendations on strategy and implementation go to the people who run the company, and they shape how the business executes. Your work also connects directly to our mission. Financial inclusion only works if the people we serve can trust us with what they share, and you would be one of the people who keeps that trust earned. Because the role spans the whole group, you would also see patterns that no single market team can: where the same gap appears in several places, and where one fix can protect every customer at once. What you'll bring Qualified lawyer with extensive, progressive experience in data protection and privacy compliance, including running privacy operations end to end: data protection impact assessments, transfer impact assessments, vendor assessments and risk management. Detailed command of data protection law across our six markets , paired with a sound understanding of information systems, data processing operations and security needs, so you can challenge the architecture as confidently as the contract. Demonstrable experience developing policies, guidelines and template clauses for the processing of personal data, and proficiency in using AI tools responsibly to support privacy research, compliance work and risk assessment. A recognised privacy or security certification (CIPP, CIPT, or ISO 27001 or 27701 implementer or auditor) is an added advantage. It is not a gate. What you'll actually do Run the programme and fix what you find. Lead remediation and data audits, conduct DPIAs, identify where we are partially or fully non-compliant, and put it right across all six markets, while keeping the records of processing that prove it. Build the tools everyone else uses. Write the guidelines, template clauses and contracts that govern how partners, suppliers and vendors handle personal information, and support the privacy software, incident response and breach notification procedures behind them. Turn the law into culture. Design training and internal communications for staff, run awareness for third parties, and support due diligence, certification, audits and new-market expansion, so data protection is something every team does rather than something Legal does to them. The reality check This role is demanding. You will hold six regimes in your head at once, advise colleagues who would rather hear a different answer, and move a business forward with clear, plain-English advice. It is an onsite role, and your calendar will hold the strategic and the urgent in the same week: a policy redesign on Monday, a vendor assessment on Wednesday, a breach notification drill on Friday. The work rewards people who like building systems that still work when nobody is watching. You're probably ready for exactly this. Ready to build the privacy standard 10 million customers can rely on? If you read the question at the top of this page and felt something, that is probably the signal. Let's talk. Why M-KOPA? At M-KOPA, we empower our people to own their careers through diverse development programs, coaching partnerships, and on-the-job training. We support individual journeys with family-friendly policies, prioritize well-being, and embrace flexibility. Join us in shaping the future of M-KOPA as we grow together. Explore more at m-kopa.com . Recognized four times by the Financial Times as one Africa's fastest growing companies (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), named on CNBC's World’s Top Fintech Companies 2025 & 2026 and by TIME100 Most influential companies in the world 2023 and 2024 , we've served over 10 million customers, unlocking $2 billion in cumulative credit for the everyday earners across Africa, in addition to over 10,000 e-bikes financed in Kenya. About The AI Whistleblower Initiative (https://aiwi.org) is an independent non-profit supporting frontier AI insiders who want to raise concerns. External: insiders and coalition members. Security engineering (full-time track only). Deep knowledge of secure platforms (e.g., able to explain the security differences between Signal and SimpleX, or between Qubes and Tails). Proficiency in operational security, threat modeling, and risk management. Familiarity with IDS, ITM, and DLP suites, and how to safeguard whistleblowers against these systems. Experience drafting, enacting, and enforcing internal security controls and policies. Knowledge of document, audio, and video watermarking systems, and counter-forensics. Genuine, demonstrable commitment to AI safety and whistleblower protection. 5-15 years experience, dependent on the projects you have worked on. Additional for the full-time profile Hands-on experience as a security engineer or builder, with a track record of shipping security tooling and infrastructure. Strong coding skills in one or more of Python, Go, Rust, or C/C++, plus shell. You write security tooling, automation, and detections yourself, without relying on AI tools. Offensive security experience (penetration testing, red teaming, exploit understanding). You can think and operate like an attacker. Infrastructure security: Linux hardening, network segmentation, cloud and self-hosted setups, IaC (Ansible, OpenTofu, etc.). Application security: secure code review, OWASP Top 10, supply-chain security, secrets management. Detection and response: logging, SIEM/IDS, forensics, incident handling. Benefits Package for full-time £120,000 base Up to 9% on UEL pension contribution 25 days of annual leave plus public bank holidays Paid parental leave Professional development budget A home office or equipment stipend for hybrid staff Wellness budget Paid for co-working space in London/SF Flexible scheduling; occasional out-of-hours work required Why join? Work as part of an ambitious team committed to a high leverage intervention: A single whistleblower disclosure can move the world if handled well. We get up every morning to make it go well. Work on a vast breadth of technological challenges and varying project sizes. Ownership and responsibility from day 1. Chance to define your personal career development. Coaching by an AIWI co-founder, now board member and serial entrepreneur/CTO as well as close collaboration with an extremely experienced Principal Engineer. Who you’d be joining: AIWI is an independent non-profit launched in late 2024. We are ~4 team members today and are scaling to ~15 within the year, spread across the Bay Area, DC, and London. Joining now, you will significantly shape what the future of AI insider support looks like. We are funded until 2029. Examples of our work to date: Policy: We pushed for and shaped the EU AI Office's channel, the world's first AI whistleblowing channel. In the US, we support the federal AI Whistleblower Protection Act and have provided expert research input on implementing SB 53's incident reporting mechanisms through a research coalition, which we helped set up. Read our work in Tech Policy Press, the Institute for Law & AI, and Transformer, and see our AI Whistleblowing Law Best Practice Guide. Insider education & support: Our online campaigns have reached thousands of company employees. We produce guides (available upon request), online courses, and help establish connections to our great partner attorneys and support (e.g. on legal advice and defense funding). Advocacy: Anthropic published its whistleblowing policy and OpenAI strengthened theirs following our Publish Your Policies Campaign. Network: We closely collaborate with the world's leading whistleblowing and AI organizations. Our ambition is to ensure that each insider disclosure is maximally impactful and safe for the person making the disclosure. Joining us means dedicating yourself to achieving that goal with us. Together, we’re unlocking new possibilities as one global team.</p></div><h2><strong>About the role</strong></h2> <p>We are looking for an experienced <strong>Senior Payroll Analyst</strong> to join our Global Payroll team and play a key role in the delivery and continuous improvement of payroll across our international markets.</p> <p>This is a senior operational role with responsibility for overseeing payroll activity across multiple countries. You will bring strong payroll expertise, sound judgement and a proactive approach to ensure employees are paid accurately, on time and in compliance with local legislation.</p> <p>Working closely with the Payroll Team, internal HR and People teams, Finance, Tax and external payroll providers, you will take ownership of complex payroll activities, provide subject-matter expertise and act as a key escalation point for payroll issues.</p> <p>The role will also provide opportunities to support <strong>international payroll projects, process improvements, system implementations and automation</strong>, helping Deliveroo build a scalable and efficient global payroll operation.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll be doing</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Take ownership of the <strong>end-to-end payroll delivery</strong> for assigned international entities.</li> <li>Partner with local HR, People Operations, Finance and Tax teams to ensure payroll inputs are complete, accurate and delivered within agreed timelines.</li> <li>Review, validate and approve payroll inputs and outputs, identifying discrepancies, trends and potential risks before payroll is finalised.</li> <li>Apply a strong understanding of <strong>legislation across multiple jurisdictions, statutory requirements and payroll practices</strong>, ensuring processes remain compliant and appropriately controlled.</li> <li>Work closely with external payroll providers, holding them accountable for <strong>accuracy, timeliness, compliance and service delivery</strong>.</li> <li>Act as a senior escalation point for complex employee and stakeholder payroll queries, providing clear guidance and appropriate resolutions.</li> <li>Perform and oversee payroll reconciliations, payment validation and statutory submissions, ensuring appropriate controls are completed and documented.</li> <li>Analyse payroll data and reporting to identify anomalies, control weaknesses, recurring issues and opportunities for improvement.</li> <li>Maintain strong payroll governance and documentation, ensuring processes, controls and procedures are consistently followed.</li> <li>Proactively identify opportunities to <strong>simplify, standardise and automate payroll processes</strong>, reducing manual intervention and operational risk.</li> <li>Support and lead payroll-related projects, including <strong>system implementations, payroll migrations, integrations, process changes and new entity onboarding</strong>.</li> <li>Partner with Technology and payroll vendors to troubleshoot system and integration issues and support effective resolution.</li> <li>Contribute to the development of payroll policies, procedures, controls and best practices across international markets.</li> <li>Share knowledge and provide guidance to Payroll Analysts and other team members, helping to build capability and consistency across the wider team.</li> <li>Stay up to date with changes to payroll legislation and communicate relevant impacts to internal stakeholders and payroll providers.</li> <li>Support the Payroll Lead with wider global payroll initiatives and deputise where required.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Significant experience working in a <strong>payroll analyst or senior payroll position</strong>, ideally within a complex, international organisation.</li> <li>Strong hands-on experience of <strong>international payroll</strong>, with experience of <strong>Italy and/or France payroll highly desirable</strong>.</li> <li>Good working knowledge of Italian and/or French payroll legislation, statutory requirements and payroll processes is preferable.</li> <li>Experience managing payroll across multiple countries and working with <strong>third-party payroll providers</strong>.</li> <li>Strong understanding of payroll controls, reconciliations, payments, statutory reporting and compliance.</li> <li>Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interrogate payroll data, identify discrepancies and understand the root cause of issues.</li> <li>Excellent attention to detail and a strong focus on payroll accuracy and risk management.</li> <li>Experience of identifying and implementing <strong>process improvements, automation and operational efficiencies</strong>.</li> <li>Experience supporting or leading payroll projects, system implementations or payroll migrations.</li> <li>Strong Excel skills and confidence working with payroll data and reporting.</li> <li>Experience with <strong>Workday/Cloudpay</strong> or other HR/payroll technology is preferred.</li> <li>Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to challenge, influence and provide a clear point of view.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex payroll matters clearly to both payroll and non-payroll stakeholders.</li> <li>A proactive, solutions-focused approach and the confidence to question <strong>the why and the how</strong> behind existing processes.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Why Deliveroo?</strong></h2> <p>Deliveroo’s mission is to build the definitive food company by making food more convenient and accessible.</p> <p>As a technology-driven business in one of the world’s fastest-growing industries, Deliveroo offers the opportunity to make a real impact while working in a fast-paced and innovative environment.</p> <p>Deliveroo also offers a wide range of competitive benefits across health, family, finance, community, convenience, growth, time away and relocation.</p> <h2><strong>Workplace and diversity</strong></h2> <p>Deliveroo is committed to building a workplace that reflects the diversity of the world around us and where everyone can belong.</p> <p>There is no judgement when it comes to the things that make people who they are — whether that is gender, race, sexuality, religion or even a secret aversion to coriander.</p> <p>If you are passionate about food and excited to help shape one of the fastest-growing companies in an exciting space, Deliveroo would love to hear from you.</p> <p> </p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Diversity, Equity and Inclusion</strong><br><br>At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We’re committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong.</p> <p>We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief.</p> <p>If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you’ll have the opportunity to let us know once you’ve submitted your application. We’ll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience.</p> <p>If you’re excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we’d love to hear from you!</p> <p><strong>Privacy</strong></p> <p>Deliveroo will process your personal information in accordance with our <span><a href="https://careers.deliveroo.co.uk/privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Candidate Privacy Policy</a></span>.</p> <p><em data-renderer-mark="true"><br>Beware of recruitment scams: DASH Brands will never ask you to pay money or share sensitive financial information during hiring — learn more about DASH Brands' legitimate recruiting process at</em> <a class="_ymio1r31 _ypr0glyw _zcxs1o36 _mizu194a _1ah3dkaa _ra3xnqa1 _128mdkaa _1cvmnqa1 _4davt94y _4bfu18uv _1hms8stv _ajmmnqa1 _vchhusvi _kqswh2mm _2rkolb4i _ect4ttxp _syaz13af _1a3b18uv _4fpr8stv _5goinqa1 _f8pj13af _9oik18uv _1bnxglyw _jf4cnqa1 _30l313af _1nrm18uv _c2waglyw _1iohnqa1 _9h8h12zz _10531ra0 _1ien1ra0 _n0fx1ra0 _1vhv17z1" href="http://careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness" data-renderer-mark="true" data-is-router-link="false" data-testid="link-with-safety"><em data-renderer-mark="true">careersatdoordash.com/recruitment-scam-awareness</em></a><em data-renderer-mark="true">.</em></p></div> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Consultant/Senior Consultant, Data & AI Strategy & Governance
description: <div class="content-intro"><h3><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142); font-family: helvetica, arial, sans-serif;">About Baringa </span></h3> <p>Baringa is a global consulting firm that partners with leaders to drive change and create value. With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.</p> <p>The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.</p> <p>Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. The firm is known for its kind, curious experts who listen closely and care deeply about client success as they help clients transform energy markets, modernise financial platforms, expand telecoms and digital networks through advanced data analytics, enable digital services in government, and unlock growth in consumer sectors.</p> <p>Certified as a <em>Great Place to Work </em>around the world, Baringa has been recognised by the <em>Financial Times </em>in 22 categories of its UK Leading Management Consultants rankings, and by <em>Forbes </em>for four consecutive years as one of the World’s Best Management Consulting Firms.</p></div><h2><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"><span data-contrast="none">Our Data, AI, Solutions and Engineering practice are looking for experienced Consultants and Senior Consultants to join the team.</span> </span></h2> <p><span class="TextRun SCXW86075854 BCX8" lang="EN-GB" data-contrast="auto"><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW86075854 BCX8">Our Data, AI, Solutions & </span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW86075854 BCX8">Engineering team</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW86075854 BCX8"> really likes helping our clients solve their complex problems with data, by implementing controls and governance of data, creating actionable insights, embedding machine learning solutions or building data platforms. We bring the right team and skills on the table and can offer deep </span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW86075854 BCX8">expertise</span><span class="NormalTextRun SCXW86075854 BCX8"> across Data Strategy, Data Science & Engineering, Data Visualisation, Data Management, Data Architecture and Software Development.</span></span><span class="EOP Selected SCXW86075854 BCX8" data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <h3><span style="color: rgb(0, 53, 142);"><span data-contrast="none">What you will be doing</span></span></h3> <p><span data-contrast="auto">You will be using your experience to help our clients solve their most important data challenges. </span><span data-contrast="auto">Data and AI strategy and governance</span><span data-contrast="auto"> call on very similar skills, and you will bring both: understanding what the business is trying to achieve, shaping a clear data vision and business case, and putting in place the right data foundations.</span> <span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">You will also support the growth of our team, helping them to build the skills they need to solve our clients’ challenges. Depending on your level, you will have the opportunity to help shape the direction of the practice, grow the business and lead our people.</span><span data-ccp-props="{"201341983":0,"335559739":0,"335559740":240}"> </span></p> <p><span data-contrast="auto">Most of our engagements span both strategy and governance. title: Junior Python Software Engineer
description: About Abound We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation. And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch. Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us. About the role We’re looking for a Junior Software Engineer to join our New Products & Geographies Engineering team in London. This team launches and scales new lending propositions in two directions: bringing Abound’s lending to customers in new countries and expanding our B2B offering for partners. We move quickly, exploring ideas through production-ready MVPs and iterating as products mature. This is a hybrid role, with at least three days a week in our London office. It’s a great opportunity for someone early in their career who wants to grow quickly, work on real production systems, and learn how a high-growth fintech operates from the inside. You’ll work alongside experienced engineers who will support you through code reviews, pairing, and mentorship. We value engineers who are curious about the business and are keen to work with stakeholders to improve processes and customer experience. Our technology stack Python (including FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, procrastinate, SQLAlchemy and Uvicorn), Postgres, MySQL, Liquibase, Retool, Docker and AWS. What you’ll be doing: Build and maintain features in our backend services, which can span any part of the lending lifecycle – from finding and onboarding new customers, to helping underwriters assess affordability, through to paying out and collecting loans Take part in the full software development lifecycle: contributing to designs, writing tests, reviewing code and helping with deployments Write clean, well-tested Python, with guidance and feedback from senior engineers Work with colleagues in Product and Design, as well as internal users, to understand requirements and turn them into working software Work closely with our React frontend developers to build the APIs and backend logic their features rely on Write and improve SQL queries against our Postgres databases Help troubleshoot and resolve system issues that affect our customers Gradually take ownership of parts of the platform as your experience grows Who you are: You’ll need: 0–2 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent experience from a degree, bootcamp, internships or personal projects Working knowledge of Python – you don’t need to be an expert, but you’re comfortable writing, testing and debugging code An understanding of core programming concepts such as data structures, object-oriented design and unit testing Familiarity with SQL, relational databases and Git To be able to work from our London office at least three days a week You’ll do well here if you: Have a sharp eye for detail – in lending, small mistakes can have a real impact on customers Learn quickly, take initiative and work methodically through problems, even in a large, evolving codebase Communicate clearly, ask questions, take on feedback and work well in a team Have a genuine interest in fintech and how financial products work Ideally you'll also have: Experience with async Python or frameworks such as FastAPI Basic familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP or Azure) or Docker Knowledge of lending products or open banking How we work: To be successful here, our culture needs to energies you. Here’s how we operate: High bar and real ownership: We’re a high-performing team, and we hire people who raise the bar and take pride in great work. We own outcomes, not tasks. Focus on impact: We measure success by what we deliver to customers. We prioritise carefully so our energy goes where it makes the biggest difference. MVP and iteration culture: We ship fast, learn from real customers, and continuously improve our products and processes. One team collaboration: We collaborate closely across engineering, product, operations and the wider business. Thrive in change: Priorities evolve as we learn what works. We value people who use good judgement, adapt quickly, and stay focused on outcomes. What we offer: Equity – everyone owns a piece of the company Hybrid working, with three days a week in the office 25 days’ holiday a year, plus 8 bank holidays 2 paid volunteering days a year A one-month paid sabbatical after 4 years Employee loan Free gym membership through WellHub A team wellness budget to be active together – set up a yoga class, a tennis lesson or go bouldering Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Engineering Lead - Sports Platform
description: 🚀 Why Midnite? Midnite is a next-generation sports betting and gaming platform built for a new wave of players. We combine sharp product thinking, bold brand, and fast execution to create experiences that feel modern, intuitive, and built for how people actually play today. Over 400,000 players have already made the move, and we’re only just getting started. We’re a high-performance team operating at pace. High ownership. Constant iteration. No hiding behind processes. We move quickly, test relentlessly, and turn ambitious ideas into real impact. If you’re driven, creative, and thrive in fast-moving environments where you can shape meaningful outcomes - keep reading. Not your grandad’s bookie. The Sports Group owns Midnite’s sportsbook experience - from discovering sports and markets to building, placing and tracking bets, cashing out and settlement. We build customer-facing products, critical backend services and the trading and operational tools that power them, working closely with Product, Design and Trading to expand our sports offering and make complex, real-time betting systems feel simple, fast and reliable. Within the group, the Sportsbook Platform team is modernising the tools behind that experience through an improved back office and practical use of AI, helping our trading team work more efficiently, reduce manual effort and gain greater control over the sportsbook. We’re looking for an Engineering Lead to provide hands-on technical leadership while formally managing and developing a team of three to four engineers. This is not a conventional Engineering Manager role or a purely technical lead position: you’ll create PRs, write production code and release features while setting technical direction and helping the whole team perform at its best. You’ll bring deep backend experience and a full-stack, systems-thinking mindset, understanding how clients, APIs, services, data, infrastructure, operations and third-party integrations work together. You’ll work closely with Product, Design and the trading team to turn complex or ambiguous problems into simple, reliable experiences delivered incrementally. Your impact will be measured not only by what you build, but by the quality of the team’s technical decisions, delivery and growth. You will: Technical direction: Set pragmatic technical direction and lead system design across clients, APIs, services, data, infrastructure and integrations. Hands-on engineering: Create PRs, write production code and release features, alongside contributing technical designs, investigations and reviews. Product delivery: Work with Product and Design to turn ambiguous opportunities into clear milestones, small deliverables and frequent releases. People leadership: Manage three to four engineers through clear expectations, one-to-ones, feedback, performance management and development support. Coaching: Develop engineers through design discussions, reviews, pairing, debugging and production incidents without becoming a bottleneck. Engineering quality: Champion effective testing, observability, safe releases and strong production feedback loops. Technical judgement: Make sensible trade-offs, keep risks visible and help the team improve systems following production problems. Wider contribution: Use AI responsibly and contribute to hiring, onboarding and shared engineering practices. The next Midniter: Significant backend engineering experience, including time operating at senior or lead level. Deep backend expertise with a full-stack, systems-thinking mindset across clients, APIs, services, data, infrastructure and operations. Strong Python skills, or experience with another modern backend language and a willingness to learn Python. Experience setting technical direction and designing, delivering and operating reliable systems. Experience in formally managing engineers, or strong evidence of readiness to own one-to-ones, feedback, performance and development for a team of three to four. Challenge assumptions constructively, helping Product and Design find simpler or more effective ways to achieve the intended outcome and the ability to break ambiguous, complex work into simple, safe deliverables. Solid database and production-engineering fundamentals, including AWS, CI/CD and observability. You communicate with energy and clarity, bring others into technical discussions, and help create momentum across the team. 💰 Winnings Private health insurance with zero excess, including optical cover and optional dental. Income protection to protect your earnings and give you peace of mind. Tenure holiday policy. After three years you receive an extra two days leave, increasing to 30 days annually after five years. Flexible working and a fully supported home office setup so you can do your best work from home. Nursery salary sacrifice scheme helping parents save thousands each year on nursery fees. Salary sacrifice schemes for tech and holidays so you can spread the cost of the things you want. Retail discounts and subscription perks across a wide range of brands. Quarterly team socials to connect, celebrate and have fun together. At Midnite, we’re committed to creating equal opportunities for everyone. title: Engineering Lead - Security
description: About 9fin 9fin is the AI platform powering global debt markets — the world’s largest asset class at over $145 trillion. Debt markets are vast, global, and mission-critical, yet still run on fragmented data, PDFs, and manual workflows. 9fin replaces this broken infrastructure with a single platform that centralises proprietary credit data, deep analysis, and high-value workflows across global markets. Today, 9fin powers teams at 300+ blue-chip institutions worldwide, including global banks, asset managers, private equity firms, law firms, and advisors. The business is scaling at exceptional speed, with rapid expansion in the US and best-in-class retention driven by deep workflow adoption. We’re at a defining inflection point. With proven product-market fit and strong, global market pull, 9fin is accelerating toward becoming the category-defining platform for debt markets worldwide. The role We’re hiring a Security Engineering Lead to build and lead our security engineering team, reporting to the Head of Platform. You’ll manage engineers working across product and platform security, set a clear direction for the function and help us grow our product security capability. You’ll join a small team with both specialisms already represented and shape how it develops. Our product security engineers work alongside Product Engineering teams, contributing to planning, design, code and delivery. They report to you for technical development, performance and career progression. You’ll stay close enough to their work to support them well, even when you are not part of their day-to-day team. You’ll bring experience as a security engineer and as a people manager. You should be able to challenge a design, reason through a threat model and help an engineer find a practical solution. You’ll also need to make choices about where we invest, build relationships across engineering and explain security priorities in terms of customer and business risk. What you’ll do Lead and develop our product and platform security engineers through regular feedback, coaching, clear expectations and fair performance assessment. Build a focused security engineering strategy and roadmap, informed by our products, engineering plans and the risks that matter most. Grow the team thoughtfully, identifying capability gaps and taking responsibility for hiring and onboarding. Agree sustained product security placements with engineering leaders, with clear priorities, useful feedback and a strong connection to the security team. Help teams build security into architecture and implementation, including access control, tenant isolation, confidential data handling and AI systems. Work with Platform Engineering to make secure infrastructure and delivery practices easy to adopt, using shared controls and automation where they help. Stay involved in important technical decisions through design and code reviews, investigations and selective implementation. Help engineers raise concerns and resolve disagreements constructively. Make material risks and trade-offs clear to the leaders accountable for the decision. Partner with IT and Information Security on shared risks, incident response and assurance requirements. Measure whether our approach reduces meaningful risk and helps engineers deliver securely. Use what we learn to improve it. What we’re looking for A background in hands-on security engineering, with strong product or application security experience. Demonstrated line management experience: developing engineers, giving difficult feedback, assessing performance and supporting career progression. Experience supporting engineers whose daily work happens within other teams, or comparable evidence of managing effectively without observing all their work directly. Current technical judgement across secure software design, threat modelling, authentication, authorisation and protection of sensitive data. Enough cloud and platform security breadth to guide specialists and make sound decisions across both areas. Experience setting priorities and securing support for security improvements across engineering teams. The ability to explain risk clearly, offer workable options and make proportionate recommendations under uncertainty. A collaborative approach that helps product and platform engineers own the security of the systems they build. You should be comfortable reading and reviewing production code and discussing implementation choices. The role combines technical leadership with people management and responsibility for building the function. Useful experience Working with AWS, backend services, infrastructure as code and automated delivery. Securing multi-tenant products, confidential customer data or AI-enabled systems. Building or improving a small security engineering team in a growing organisation. Introducing secure patterns or tooling that engineers adopted and continued to use. We value evidence of sound judgement and useful outcomes. You do not need experience with every technology we use. What success looks like During your first months, you’ll understand the team’s strengths, our main risks and how security work gets done. You’ll agree development plans with the engineers and establish clear working relationships with Product Engineering, Platform and Information Security. Over the following months, you’ll put a prioritised roadmap and a workable embedded model in place. Teams should involve security earlier in important decisions, engineers should have useful technical support, and the highest-priority improvements should have clear owners and delivery capacity. As the function grows, we’ll look for evidence of better protection for customers, adoption of secure engineering practices and a team whose engineers are developing in their roles. Hybrid Policy 9fin is a hybrid company, and the office is a regular part of how we work. From January 2027, all employees will work from their designated 9fin office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays. Some teams may be asked to be in the office more often, where the nature of their work calls for it. For the rest of the week, you may work from wherever works best for you and your team. Your Talent Partner will share hybrid working details for this role. 9fin is an equal opportunities employer At 9fin we are dedicated to building and promoting a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone can reach their full potential and truly belong. We recognize that building diverse teams enables a more creative and productive environment. If you’re excited about this role but your experience doesn’t perfectly align with the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. title: GTM Engineer
description: Can you help us fix the world's most broken supply chain? The fashion industry produces over 100 billion garments a year. 60% end up in landfill, not because people don't want these clothes, but because the supply chain that moves them from donation to resale is offline, manual and broken. Fleek is fixing this. Our mission is to make secondhand the first choice. We run a B2B marketplace where resellers and stores buy clothing in bulk, and we build the AI systems that digitise the supply chain behind it. Our buyers sell on eBay, Vinted, Depop, Whatnot, eBay Live and TikTok Shop, or run vintage stores from Brick Lane to Paris to New York. They source graded stock from wholesalers and rag houses across many countries. Our key enabler is FleekSort, an AI model fine-tuned on secondhand fashion that can grade, price and categorise an item from a single photo. We are now going well beyond vintage. Live sellers can sell almost anything, and there is an opportunity for Fleek to be the backend for B2B resale. We've now started onboarding customers alongside supply from Japan, South Korea, the Philippines and Thailand. Since 2022, we've saved 9 million items from landfill and tripled in size year on year. We've raised ~$50M from a16z, Y Combinator, HV Capital and others, and recently closed our Series B. Our advisors and private investors include operators behind Depop, Shopify and Postmates. We're looking for people who want to build something that matters, and move fast doing it. About the role You'll join the GTM team as our GTM Engineer, reporting to our GTM lead and working day to day with the new business team. You'll own the system we use to find and win customers, on both sides of the marketplace. On the demand side, that means online resellers, live sellers and physical stores in the UK, Europe and the US, buying vintage, deadstock, new with tags and luxury. On the supply side, it means the brands, brokers, wholesalers and rag houses who sell to them. As we add new categories and markets, the system has to find those customers too. We already have pipelines that scrape marketplaces and load leads into our CRM. The next step is everything after that: putting the right leads first, reaching them well, and learning from every outcome. You'll own the engine end to end, from the first scrape to the revenue each new customer brings in. This is not a typical B2B SaaS GTM engineering role. You won't spend your days wiring a CRM to a LinkedIn sequencer or building dashboards. Everyone on our commercial team builds their own tools with AI. You'll take on the problems they can't: systems that improve themselves, infrastructure that scales, and outreach that works within limits set by platforms like Meta. The role is part engineer, part product manager and part commercial. You won't carry a closes target, but you'll own every metric that moves it. The problem you'll solve We want a system that finds the right customers, puts them in order, reaches out, and gets better every week. It runs as a loop: Find. Source leads across marketplaces and social platforms, for every segment and market we sell into. Prioritise. Score each lead on the signals that predict a good customer, not just a likely reply. Reach out. Contact them on Instagram, WhatsApp, email, phone or LinkedIn, personalised by AI and handed to a rep at the right moment. Learn. Feed every outcome back into scoring. If a store replied but wasn't a fit, similar leads drop down the list, so we stop spending tokens and rep time on them. Then back to step 1. To make that loop work, you'll build a second brain for GTM: one layer that holds everything we know about a customer, with models and agents running on top. That includes the messages we sent and how they replied, how fast they replied and closed, what they sell and where, what they click and search for in our app, what they told our reps on calls, and how much they spend and how well they retain. The same data powers our account management team, who look after customers once they've placed their first orders. Matching each buyer with the right supply is one of their next big problems, and you'll help solve it. What you'll do Own the acquisition engine. Learn how our current pipelines work and improve them. If a rebuild is the right call, make the case for it, and keep leads flowing to the reps while you build. Source at scale in new segments. Find vintage stores, live sellers, deadstock and luxury buyers, and new suppliers, in every market we enter. Build the scoring and feedback loop. Define what a good lead looks like for each segment, then keep refining it on what actually closes and what actually spends. Engineer multi-channel outreach. Instagram, WhatsApp, email, calls and LinkedIn, personalised by AI and built around real limits like Instagram DM caps and Meta restrictions. Own the funnel numbers. Leads sourced per day on each platform, reply rate, conversion rate and GMV per close by source. Use them to decide what to fix next. Sit with the reps and talk to customers. Learn why a lead is good and how each segment wants to be sold to. Then automate the repetitive parts of the rep's day. Turn repeat work into agents. Qualification, first messages, reply handling, dedupe and CRM hygiene should run without a person. Keep it efficient. Every system you build should make sense on cost per lead and unit economics. Connect acquisition to retention. Make sure new customers land cleanly with account management, and help build the buyer-to-supply matching they rely on. What you bring A strong technical background. You've built and run real systems, such as data pipelines, scrapers, models or production infrastructure. You've done more than configure tools. An AI-first mindset, a step ahead. You build with Claude and other models every day and know where agents work and where they break. Our commercial team is very AI-literate, and you'll push them further. Curiosity about the customer. You want to know why one lead closes and another doesn't, and how each segment wants to be sold to. You're happy on a call with a reseller. Problem solving over playbooks. You take an ambiguous problem, form your own view and ship something that works. We'd rather hire someone who works it out than someone repeating what worked elsewhere. Ownership. You challenge how things are done, bring your own recommendations and explain why. Rigour with numbers. You track honest metrics, know where your funnel leaks and judge your systems on results. Excitement about the space. You see how big the opportunity is and want to build it. Nice to have GTM, growth or RevOps experience, including outbound you've run yourself Founder or early-startup experience where you owned growth end to end Experience building ranking, scoring or recommendation models Experience building for marketplaces, resellers, live selling or independent retail Familiarity with secondhand, vintage, deadstock or luxury fashion Running multi-channel outbound under platform limits (DM caps, deliverability, warm-up) What good looks like First 30 days: you know the current pipelines inside out, have sat with the reps and have shipped your first improvements, with leads still flowing. You've shared your plan to improve what's there or rebuild it, and why. 3 months: one data layer joins outreach, replies, closes, app activity, call notes and spend. Scoring runs on it, and the loop from outcome back to scoring is live for at least one segment. 6 months: the system improves itself. Each week it sources more leads, and better ones, across our segments and markets, and conversion and GMV per close are rising. 12 months: the engine is the backbone of acquisition across vintage, deadstock and luxury, on both demand and supply. Agents run the repeat work, and you focus on what to build next. What you'll get Competitive salary plus a performance bonus tied to qualified pipeline Generous equity: being on Fleek means you'll own a part of it Comprehensive healthcare coverage A collaborative team in a lovely office in the heart of East London Access to founders. We're a small team and they're heavily involved (and good fun!) Exclusive employee discounts to buy on Fleek Access to borrow any item from our collection of vintage and reworks in the office A disproportionate level of responsibility and the chance to drive massive impact How we work High ownership, non-hierarchical and fast-moving. We hire problem solvers, not order takers. If you have a better way to do something, and it moves the numbers at a sensible cost, go for it. Our commercial team builds its own tools, so each new hire starts more effective than the last. People who deliver get more scope quickly. You'll work embedded with the GTM team, ship fast and see your work in the pipeline within days, not quarters. The practicalities Location: London HQ, E1, Spitalfields / Shoreditch Work model: in person, with trust-based flexibility Stage: post-Series B, hyper-growth Team: a GTM team of 5 AEs in new business and 3 AMs in account management, within 100+ people across London, India and Pakistan Process: an intro call, then an in-person case study in two parts: one on the business with our GTM lead, one technical with our engineers Our values Five values shape how we work at Fleek: Dream Big and Disrupt Yourself: Push the most ambitious version of what you're building. Step out of your comfort zone. Nothing is out of reach. Absolute Ownership: The buck stops with you. Drive initiatives to completion. Experiment, learn, persevere. The job isn't done until the job is done. Curiosity Leads the Way: Don't accept anything at face value. Ask questions you don't know the answer to. That's how you innovate. Talk to the Customer: Deeply understand their challenges, motivations and ambitions. Every decision starts with the customer at the centre. Embrace Diversity: A global team building for a global supply chain. Bring your authentic self and embrace the diversity of everyone you encounter. Ready to build the infrastructure for the world's fastest-growing fashion economy? If you want to work on genuinely hard problems, with a world-class team, at a company that's tripling annually, we'd love to hear from you. title: Meridial – Senior Research Software Engineer – Image Processing
description: About Meridial Meridial is a Focused Research Organisation (FRO) with a mission to bring connectomics into the living brain. We are building a platform for longitudinal, synapse-resolution mapping of functional neural circuitry in preclinical models. Our aim is to deploy this platform for translational projects and improve drug development outcomes for disorders of the central nervous system. Meridial is a new not-for-profit FRO in the Convergent Research Ecosystem and funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency ( ARIA ). The technical challenge Our imaging platform records the activity of neurons and synapses in the living brain. The scientific value of these recordings depends on converting raw images into reliable, quantitative data. This is a demanding image processing problem. Fluorescence signals are faint, noisy and spatially overlapping; residual tissue motion and other imaging artefacts must be corrected; in addition to conventional planar frames, data may be acquired from arbitrarily shaped 3D regions or several depths at once; properties vary between signal types and experimental configurations; and the same cells and synapses must be reliably matched across imaging sessions spanning weeks. You will build a software package that addresses these challenges in two modes: real-time processing and visualisation, with latencies of tens to hundreds of milliseconds, that inform experimental decisions at the microscope, and offline pipelines that deliver maximum accuracy for scientific analysis and serve as the benchmark for the real-time methods. The impact of this work is direct and visible: your software will be used at the microscope as experiments unfold, and your pipelines will generate the data underpinning new insights into how neural circuits function and how they change in disease. Key responsibilities You will own Meridial’s image processing software end to end, starting from the interface with microscope control and acquisition all the way to processed results prepared for biological analysis. This is a role with a high degree of autonomy: you will make the main design and technology decisions, set priorities with the people who use the software, and work out what to build as requirements emerge. Who you will work with Experimental team. The neuroscientists running experiments are the main users of the real-time tools. You will work with them at the microscope, understand their problems and turn joint solutions into reliable tools. Senior Software Engineer. Develops the microscope control and image acquisition software, mostly in Rust. Your real-time code exchanges data with that software but need not be part of it. Together, you will decide how the two systems connect. Neuroscience Data Scientist. Owns Meridial’s database and the downstream scientific analysis. You will ensure processed results reach the database with a full record of how they were produced. Reporting line. You will join the Computational Team and report to its Head once appointed, and to the Director of Experimental Research until then. What you will do Build robust pipelines for motion and artefact correction, segmentation of cells and synapses, separation of overlapping signals and extraction of activity over time, adapted to different signal types. Register data from flexible 3D imaging modes to reference volumes, and build tools that find the same field of view and match cells and synapses across sessions, both live at the microscope and offline at high resolution. Develop real-time versions of these methods that keep up with streaming data, including fast identification of cells as stimulation targets. Build live visualisations and summary measures, such as rolling averages, response histograms and noise metrics, that help scientists steer experiments. Define, with the Senior Software Engineer, the interface between acquisition and processing, with a focus on throughput and low latency. Evaluate and adapt existing open-source tools, develop new methods where needed, and validate them against ground truth, using offline results as the benchmark for the real-time processing. Optimise for speed and scale, using multi-threading, GPUs or compiled languages where needed, so that processing keeps up with large and growing datasets. Write clean, tested and documented code, and set up version control, continuous integration and documentation practices for the codebase. Use AI coding assistants to work efficiently, while keeping code correct and maintainable. Plan and track work in Jira or another project management system, in short iterations with the experimental team. Turn prototypes into reproducible tools that scientists can use and that can be released as open source. The person we are looking for You are an experienced software engineer with a background in image analysis or computer vision. You enjoy hard technical problems and set high standards for correctness, performance and code quality. You like working directly with the people who use your software: understanding their problems, trying out ideas with them and turning the best into reliable tools. You enjoy building from scratch and are comfortable with the ambiguity of an early-stage organisation. As the main developer of our image processing software, you will work independently and shape how it evolves. Experience in any of these areas would help you hit the ground running, but none is required: real-time or streaming data processing, microscopy or scientific image analysis, statistics, or machine learning for image analysis. A background in biology, biophysics or neuroscience would also help. Essential experience Experience with image analysis or computer vision, such as segmentation, motion correction, registration or denoising, including image quality measures like signal-to-noise ratio. 5+ years of software development experience, in industry or research (for example, PhD or postdoctoral work where software was a main output). Strong proficiency in Python, with good engineering practice: Git, automated testing and well-documented code. Experience with performance optimisation, such as multi-threading or GPU programming, and with a compiled language such as C/C++ or Rust (if not Rust, a willingness to learn it). Experience building interactive, high-performance data visualisations. Experience building data-intensive pipelines for large datasets, from requirements through to deployment. Experience working directly with end users who are not developers, gathering requirements and turning feedback into improvements. Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants in your day-to-day development. Physical demands Fine motor skills for operating computers and office/lab equipment Ability to move light-to-moderately heavy items (typical lab supplies/equipment); may include occasional lifting/carrying with appropriate equipment (e.g., carts/dollies) Position type / schedule Start date: February 2027 or later. Full-time. Based in London, with an on-site presence of four days per week. Additional information Please send your CV. We will ask for two references during the interview process. Generous benefits will be communicated during interviews. For exceptional candidates, Meridial will consider visa sponsorship and relocation support.
