title: Applied AI - Member of Technical Staff
description: About Us We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity. Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next. The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve. Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost. Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor. In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence. We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you. About the Role Applied AI Research at Callosum discovers the methods that make real AI workloads faster, cheaper and better, and turns them into systems that run in production. You will study how agentic workflows, retrieval pipelines and code intelligence stacks actually behave, then invent ways to optimise them at a systems level. A single optimisation can touch agent and workflow design, context and prompting, model choice, the serving stack and the silicon underneath. So we don't hire specialists in one layer. We hire researchers who can reason across the whole system, from agentic design down to the specifics of the model, and who have a feel for how inference and hardware shape what is possible. The role is research-led and engineering-heavy. You will need first-principles judgment to see what kind of system a problem needs, the rigour to prove that it works, and the engineering skill to build it yourself. You will sit across our research and platform functions. What you discover becomes product capability, and what you see in real workloads sets the research agenda. We run a flat Member of Technical Staff structure. Responsibility and scope grow with what you demonstrate, including leadership of the Applied AI Research function as the team scales. What You'll Work On Our research tries to construct optimal inference systems from the silicon layer all the way up to the harness: the system will learn from the actual deployment profile and tasks it is used on and optimise itself. Open problems you will own include: •⁠ ⁠ Reverse-engineering agentic systems. Infer the structure of agentic systems from minimal data, and find where it spends compute it doesn't need to. •⁠ ⁠ Routing. Build robust routers that send each request to the cheapest or fastest path that strictly matches or beats the incumbent model on quality. •⁠ ⁠ Proving there is no regression. Design layered proxy evaluations, that bound quality ever more tightly, from coarse checks down to a granular understanding of the system. •⁠ ⁠ New optimisation surface area. Extend the same automatic, detection to new optimisation techniques, and help decide which ones we pursue next. •⁠ ⁠ Research that ships. Run rigorous experiments, write up what you learn, and work with our platform team to turn what works into general product capability. •⁠ ⁠ Shared research infrastructure. Build the evaluation harnesses, benchmarks and experiment tooling the team runs on. How We Work •⁠ ⁠ Generalists by design. Our cadence is fast and our priorities move as we learn. You will move between projects as the problem demands, so breadth and the speed at which you learn matter more than depth in one niche. •⁠ ⁠ Research judged by production. A result counts when it holds on real workloads. Ideas move quickly from hypothesis to experiment to a deployed system. •⁠ ⁠ Close to real workloads. You work from real production systems and pipelines. Customer contact is scoped: team members who show an aptitude for it can take on more customer-facing technical work, but it is not the core of the role. •⁠ ⁠ A mix of experience. We hire across seniority levels. Experienced researchers bring proven practice from large-scale AI development, earlier-career members bring speed and fresh eyes, and each learns from the other. What You Bring •⁠ ⁠Broad, foundational knowledge across the modern AI stack: agent and workflow design, LLMs and how they work inside, and inference and serving. You can reason about how a change in one layer affects the others. •⁠ ⁠Exceptional technical depth, demonstrated through any of: research that shipped, production AI systems at scale, or an early or founding role where you owned the system end to end. •⁠ ⁠Rigour in experimental design, evaluation and benchmarking. You can tell a real improvement from noise, and you design the measurement before you trust the result. •⁠ ⁠A very fast learner who goes to first principles when the map runs out. •⁠ ⁠Strong engineering skills: you build the systems you research. •⁠ ⁠A bias for action, comfort with ambiguity and a strong sense of ownership. What Sets You Apart •⁠ ⁠An early or founding role at an AI-first, deep-tech company, where you made key technical decisions from first principles. •⁠ ⁠You have designed and built multi-agent or agentic systems from the ground up, and you also have depth lower in the stack. •⁠ ⁠Low-level systems or performance engineering: kernels, serving engines or latency-critical systems. •⁠ ⁠Experience of large-scale AI development at a frontier lab or big tech company, and the engineering practices that come with it. •⁠ ⁠Research in inference optimisation, model internals, evaluation, routing or distillation. •⁠ ⁠Publications, open-source work or public write-ups that show how you think. •⁠ ⁠Familiarity with novel accelerator platforms. •⁠ ⁠Experience working directly with external engineering teams. What We Offer •⁠ ⁠Competitive Salary, determined by skills and experience •⁠ ⁠Equity & Ownership •⁠ ⁠Private healthcare •⁠ ⁠We offer Visa sponsorship and relocation benefits to hire the best in the world •⁠ ⁠We work in person at our London office. You'll have the tools, space and setup to do your best work, and if you have specific needs, just tell us We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome, and believe in equal opportunities for all. title: Lead AI Security Engineer - Remote (UK Only)
description: A platform you can believe in: Immersive One is the leading cyber resilience solution across the globe. Build and scale a best in class platform alongside a team of the brightest minds in cybersecurity! At Immersive, we’re uniquely positioned to future-proof organizations against any cyber challenge. If that excites you, read on! Immersive is the cyber proving ground for the AI enterprise. Through Immersive One, organizations can test whether people, AI-enabled workflows, cyber security teams, agents, and leaders can perform securely under realistic pressure, then turn that performance into evidence they can use to improve, benchmark, and report readiness. Trusted by 30%+ of the Fortune 100 and ranked #1 in the Forrester Wave™ 2026, Immersive helps organizations prove AI can be adopted safely, teams can develop and defend at AI speed, leaders can lead through crisis, and AI agents can be validated before they are trusted in live workflows https://www.immersivelabs.com/why-immersive-labs We help the world’s biggest brands like Citi, Pfizer, Humana, and HSBC, protect their revenues and brand reputations. Immersive was founded in 2017, from a cargo container in Bristol, UK we’ve grown to over 300 employees globally, announced funding of more than $180 million and been voted a Best place to work on multiple occasions! https://www.immersivelabs.com/company/our-story Lead AI Security Engineer - (Remote within UK) Immersive is hiring! Could you be our next AI Security Engineer? Due to customer demand and increasing maturity within our platform, we have an exciting and challenging opportunity for an experienced, innovative, data-driven Cyber Security Engineer with a background in implementing security in AI products to join our Container 7 team as a Lead AI Security Engineer. We’re looking for someone with a builder mindset who enjoys creating, improving, and scaling ways of working. You’ll have full ownership and accountability for your area, with real scope to shape the role and make it your own. You’ll thrive in a small team with a broad remit, where there is plenty of opportunity to learn, develop, and grow alongside the business. As a Lead AI Security Engineer, you will be a key player in our Container 7 team, shaping and influencing the rollout of our AI & Cyber security roadmap, simulating attack paths, demonstrating how to secure infrastructure and build security into your agents and AI landscape from day one - all while helping train our users to counter the latest threats. You will be constantly researching, learning, totally geeking out on all things AI security-related, from agentic security to the latest AI-driven attacks, and then taking that knowledge and creating labs and ranges for our customers. This role would suit someone who is immersed in the AI security field and has strong insight and opinions on how our product roadmap should evolve to ensure our customers have the tools to learn how to build and deploy AI securely You will design, build, and deliver practical and theoretical content to gamify AI security and make it engaging and fun for the end user. You'll shake up traditional training and teach complex concepts in an innovative way. If you have an extensive background in cyber security - in particular AppSec and cloud security - are experienced in the area of securing AI agents and securing AI-driven platforms, and want to disrupt how employees build their resilience against the latest threats, we will appreciate your input and give you the space to innovate within our market-leading platform, Immersive One, and our new AI Security product. Your main responsibilities: Utilising knowledge of offensive & defensive appsec and cloud security engagements to plan, write and deploy AI security labs, challenges and online learning content on the Immersive One platform. Lead on the building of content around security vulnerabilities in AI and Large Language Model (LLM) deployments (e.g., prompt injection, data poisoning, model evasion). This could be multi-format content utilising various teaching methods; practical exercises, questions & gamification Test AI Security labs and ranges to ensure they function as expected Research vulnerabilities, tools, and offensive tactics and compile this research to deliver practical and theory labs to users Compile technical research into understandable, concise content for both technical and non-technical audiences Work with the wider Product team on new projects and product innovations and how best to deploy them Sounds good? We’d love to hear from you if you have proven experience in the following areas (we know it’s tough, but please try to avoid the confidence gap. You don’t have to match all the listed requirements exactly to be considered for this role): Proven and extensive experience in application security, product security, or cloud security, with a strong focus on AI/ML or LLM technologies. It would be highly desirable if you are experienced in threat modeling for LLM and agent systems, agent permission design, Guardrails and output validation, evaluation and regression testing, model drift detection, and Drift prevention Thought leader within AI Security - you’re someone who is constantly reading the latest whitepapers and thinking several sprints ahead as to what we should be building within our AI Security product roadmap. Excellent communication skills to partner and build relationships with engineering and product colleagues outside of the core security team. You’re a self-starter who is comfortable working with autonomy, takes initiative, and spots opportunities to add value. You bring a hands-on approach, with a willingness to get stuck in and support across a broad range of priorities when needed. Deep understanding of the AI threat landscape, including the OWASP Gen AI Security Project and MITRE ATLAS, as well as an understanding of adversarial machine learning techniques. You possess strong attention to detail, have a logical approach to problem-solving, and the ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment. Hold strong programming skills (e.g., Python) and familiarity with common AI/ML frameworks (e.g., PyTorch, TensorFlow, LangChain). Immersive’s growth has been fuelled by our values that underpin everything we do, here's how they relate to this role: Driven - We push the boundaries of innovation, acting swiftly to achieve ambitious outcomes. Our drive embodies a culture of ambition, where challenges are stepping stones to excellence. Inclusive - Our strength lies in diversity, fostering a culture where every individual contributes to our collective strength. We champion open dialogue and empathy, ensuring a collaborative, inclusive workplace. Customer Centric - We seek to develop deep relationships with our customers to help them achieve their business outcomes. We exceed our customers and partners' expectations by crafting products, services and experiences that surprise, delight and ensure they feel valued and supported every day. One Team - We are a talented global team working together to achieve our vision. Central to our ethos, resilience means adapting and thriving in adversity. It guides our innovation, ensuring we and our clients are prepared for the future. We encourage people of all different backgrounds and identities to apply. We are committed to maintaining an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you and do your very best work. Excited by the above? We’re ready to receive your application! As well as an inclusive, supportive place for you to be you. We offer an extensive range of benefits so you can do your very best work: Time off, flexible and remote working so you can work when is best for you, includes 25 days annual leave + 2 volunteering days and your birthday off. The longer you are with Immersive, the more holiday days you get, up to a maximum of 30 days after five years of service. Look after your family and yourself with enhanced parental leave, mindfulness groups, critical illness cover, 7% matched pension, private healthcare plan and more. Career and learning development through the platform, a dedicated professional development fund and our ‘Learn Anything’ fund - which enables you to learn anything that’s not work! Recognition & Rewards for doing great work and living our values and behaviours. Informal or formal flexible working options, e.g. flexible start and finish times, reduced hours. We have a vibrant team culture with team events throughout the year. Our socials have included everything from pottery painting and paper mask making, to dungeons and dragons! When you do visit the UK hub, getting there is easy: we’re based in the centre of Bristol, just a 10 minute walk from the train station. We also offer railcard loan and cycle scheme to buy a new bike. Find out more about life at Immersive Labs https://careers.immersivelabs.com Cyber threats wait for no one and neither should you. Apply now! If you would like to read more about what you can expect from our recruitment process, you can visit our dedicated interview process page. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Strategic Value Engineer (Presales) - London
description: Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. About the role We're hiring a Strategic Value Engineer (Presales) to shape and win enterprise ERP automation decisions: you reframe problems, quantify the cost of inaction, and prove value through tailored workshops and demos. Partnering with an AE, you own technical leadership, value articulation, and de-risking security/integration, building alignment across CFO/CIO-led buying committees. What you'll own Insight-led discovery and deal shaping Practice insight selling: challenge the customer's initial framing, introduce a sharper point of view on where value is actually trapped (exceptions, approvals, master data, controls), and reframe urgency using cost-of-inaction. Lead discovery across CFO/CIO/Shared Services/Procurement to uncover operational bottlenecks and decision friction, and translate that into a crisp target-state narrative and mutual action plan. Solution design and technical leadership Architect a tailored solution: scope, rollout approach, integration pattern, security posture, and success criteria. Run deep dives with IT/security and articulate how blp works in enterprise environments (ERP digital twin, data synchronization, governance and controls). Demos, workshops, and executive storytelling Deliver high-impact demos that map to customer workflows (P2P, AP, S2P) and prove outcomes, not features. Facilitate workshops that turn stakeholder skepticism into a tangible blueprint and path to value. Value engineering (business case support) Build a credible value narrative: labor productivity gains, cycle time reduction, compliance/control improvements, and stack simplification. Support champions and the AE with executive-ready business-case inputs, impact ranges, and rollout economics, flagging risk to the deal early rather than late. Competitive positioning Position blp against point tools and fragmented stacks (OCR/IDP/workflow/process mining/RPA) with an "end-to-end + exceptions-first" narrative. Help the deal team land a clear "why now" anchored in operational risk, ERP program success, and enterprise scale requirements. What we're looking for Must-haves 3–8+ years in Value Engineering / Presales / Solution Consulting / ERP process consulting (or equivalent in finance/procurement operations with strong customer-facing chops). Demonstrated ability to run insight-based discovery (Challenger-style): you can respectfully push back, quantify impact, and build conviction across a buying committee. Comfort with senior stakeholders (CFO/CIO/Head of Shared Services): you can lead without authority. Strong workshop facilitation and demo craft: story, structure, and objection handling. Ability to connect technical realities to business outcomes (FTE capacity, cycle time, controls, compliance risk, TCO). Strong plus SAP exposure (S/4, ECC, Public/Private Cloud) or multi-ERP environments. Finance/process knowledge: AP, invoice processing, S2P/P2P, exception handling, approvals, master data workflows. Experience competing against legacy vendors and "patchwork stacks." Language Fluent in English and another major European language, preferably German ( desirable), depending on territory. Location : London - Hybrid What you'll get A product that wins. blp's solution consistently outperforms competitors. Your job is to open more doors. Real ownership. Choose annually to take your variable compensation in cash or company shares. Growth and autonomy. Build your own success path in a rapidly scaling, internationally expanding company. Continuous learning. Structured onboarding and ongoing coaching to help you excel. Exceptional team. Join a group of ambitious, collaborative colleagues who push each other to achieve excellence. Learn more about blp and our values at blp.digital/company/careers . Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

Good negotiation skills with a track record of delivering cost savings and driving value from suppliers. A proactive, builder mindset, with the ability to design processes and establish strong internal relationships. A relevant qualification or progress towards one (e.g. CIPS). description: <p><strong>Your Impact at LILA</strong></p> <p>We're building a talent-dense, high-agency AI safety team at Lila that will engage all core teams within the organization (science, model training, lab integration, etc.), to identify and mitigate risks from scientific superintelligence while retaining the core scientific discovery capabilities of the stack. The initial focus of this team will be to build and implement a bespoke safety strategy for Lila, tailored to its specific goals and deployment strategies. This will involve technical safety strategy development, broader ecosystem engagement, safety-focused evaluations, safety systems to mitigate risks, and a research agenda that explores longer-term needs such as oversight of superintelligent scientific systems.</p> <p>We are seeking a chemist to map risk across the chemical sciences domain: you will connect deep chemistry expertise with dual-use risk assessment to help safeguard increasingly capable scientific AI. You will investigate how advances in chemical research could change harmful capabilities, including established and emerging chemical threats.</p> <p><strong>What You'll Be Building</strong></p> <ul> <li>Map chemical misuse risks across scientific models, agents and automated experimentation, connecting scientific advances to harmful applications and identifying emerging or overlooked pathways.</li> <li>Assess how scientific feasibility, practical complexity and actors' expertise or resources affect the plausibility and likelihood of misuse, including which constraints AI could change.</li> <li>Distinguish established capabilities, plausible future developments and weakly supported hypotheses, updating assessments as scientific evidence and AI capabilities evolve.</li> <li>Identify gaps in coverage, frame questions for consultants and specialist organizations, and assess and integrate their findings with support from the expert-program team.</li> <li>Translate scientific risk judgments into dual-use policy boundaries, evaluation priorities and mitigation requirements that preserve beneficial chemistry.</li> <li>Partner with threat modelers, evaluation researchers and mitigation teams to design informative assessments, interpret red-team findings and test safeguards.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You'll Need to Succeed</strong></p> <ul> <li>Deep expertise (a PhD, or comparable experience) in synthetic chemistry or a closely related discipline, demonstrated through substantial research or applied work and sound interpretation of experimental evidence. This includes a background in molecular design and medicinal chemistry, inorganic and organometallic chemistry, synthesis, process development and formulations, or other relevant sub-fields.</li> <li>Substantive experience assessing chemical dual-use risks (e.g. across national security, export controls, or other chemical risk tracking such as the CWC).</li> <li>Strong scientific judgment about feasibility, uncertainty and practical constraints, including the ability to investigate unfamiliar questions and recognize the limits of your expertise.</li> <li>The ability to identify appropriate specialists, critically assess their evidence and combine findings across disciplines into defensible risk assessments.</li> <li>Clear scientific communication, independent research judgment and an ability to collaborate across science, engineering and policy.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Bonus Points For</strong></p> <ul> <li>Prior experience applying domain expertise to AI safety through one or more of: scientific analysis informing threat models; evaluation or red-teaming work; or mitigation design.</li> <li>Experience commissioning specialist research or coordinating external scientific collaborators.</li> <li>Experience with automated chemistry, scientific modeling or the translation of computational findings into physical experiments.</li> </ul><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><strong>Compensation</strong></p> <p>We offer competitive base compensation with bonus potential and generous early-stage equity. title: Senior Researcher, Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence
description: <p><strong>FULL-TIME JOB VACANCY</strong><br><strong>Senior Researcher on Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence</strong><br><strong>Technology, Rights and Investigations Division</strong><br><strong>Multiple Office Locations Considered</strong><br><strong>Application Deadline: December 13, 2026</strong><br> <br>Human Rights Watch (HRW) is seeking a highly qualified Senior Researcher on Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence to investigate, analyze, and advocate against human rights abuses worldwide related to artificial intelligence. The role of the Senior Researcher will include documenting and conveying the rights implications of various forms of artificial intelligence and other algorithmic decision-making being developed and deployed by governments and private sector actors around the world for exclusion and repression, including  information control and censorship and discriminatory decision making, especially in high-risk contexts, for example by law enforcement and immigration authorities. Experience working on the impact of AI or other technology issues in Asia is preferred.</p> <p>The role sits in the Tech and Human Rights team within the broader Technology, Rights and Investigations Division and will report to the Deputy Director based in New York. The Senior Researcher on Human Rights and Artificial Intelligence will collaborate with other team members in the Technology, Rights and Investigations Division, and colleagues in regional and thematic divisions, and other relevant departments of HRW, including media, legal and policy team, and the advocacy department.</p> <p>The successful candidate will have deep domain expertise, as well as a track record of conducting research and investigations at the intersection of human rights abuses and AI. The role will be based in any of the following locations where HRW has an office, and will be expected to work from the office on an as-needed basis: New York, Washington DC, Los Angeles, San Francisco, Toronto, Sao Paulo, London, Brussels, Amsterdam, Berlin, Nairobi, Johannesburg, Beirut, or Stockholm. </p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Responsibilities:</strong></span><br>1. Develop a plan for strategic research and advocacy for influencing the development, application, and regulation of artificial intelligence and similar technologies by governments and the private sector to ensure respect for internationally recognized human rights, including non-discrimination and accountability;<br>2. Research, document, and analyze policies and practices related to AI, machine learning, and big data technologies that raise human rights concerns by collecting and analyzing information from a wide variety of sources, including governments, media, academia, NGOs, victims of abuses, open-source information, technologists, and others; Interview persons whose rights have been harmed by AI technologies, as well as related professionals and experts (e.g., organizations representing impacted communities, engineers who build AI technologies, data and computer scientists, etc.); <br>3. Identify and document where use of AI may have disparate impact on vulnerable or marginalized groups or may exacerbate economic inequality, and place abuses or potential for abuses within the broader political, social and economic contexts;<br>4. Write and publicize reports, op-eds, press releases, briefing memos, statements, testimony and other materials to disseminate our research findings and policy recommendations for preventing or ending human rights abuses linked to artificial intelligence applications; <br>5. Work with colleagues in the Communications Department to develop innovative multimedia and social media strategies to communicate our positions in clear and compelling ways and to advance advocacy;<br>6. Develop and implement advocacy strategies in collaboration with HRW colleagues to change or prevent abusive government laws, policies, and practices, as well as abusive corporate policies and practices; <br>7. Press companies and governments to ensure human rights protections are built into artificial intelligence by design from the outset and articulate how existing human rights standards should apply to emerging AI technologies;  <br>8. Build partnerships across key communities, including other human rights NGOs, groups representing vulnerable populations, data scientists, machine learning programmers, tech industry leaders, and academics; <br>9. Contribute to the shaping of public debates on AI around human rights internationally through clear and prompt responses to queries from policy makers, the media, colleagues, and human rights communities; <br>10. Work collaboratively with an international team of researchers within the Technology, Rights and Investigations division, including the Digital Investigations Lab, other thematic and country HRW researchers, and other relevant departments of HRW, including Communications, Legal and Policy, Advocacy, and the General Counsel’s office;<br>11. Travel domestically and internationally, as required, to conduct research, media work and advocacy; and<br>12. Be prepared and willing to work flexible hours to accommodate developing and urgent events;<br>13. Carry out other tasks as required.</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Candidate Profile </strong></span></p> <p>Candidates who are traditionally underrepresented in the technology and/or human rights sectors (such as people who identify as BIPOC, LGBTQIA+, women, migrants, people with disabilities, or people who have other related lived experiences) are enthusiastically encouraged to apply if they feel they have the ability to succeed in this role, even if they do not have all the skills and qualifications listed below.</p> <p><strong>Education:</strong> An advanced degree in journalism, law, public policy, national security, computer science, or a related field or equivalent experience is required.</p> <p><strong>Experience:</strong> A minimum of seven years of experience is required. This experience could come from a<br>variety of previous roles including, but not limited to journalists who have covered technology,<br>community activism, work at impact litigation organizations, academics, or industry professionals.</p> <p><strong>Related Skills and Knowledge</strong>:<br>1. Extensive knowledge of artificial intelligence, in particular the threats and complexities it poses to the major human rights challenges of our time is required.<br>2. Experience working on the impact of AI or other technology issues in Asia and fluency in an Asian language are desirable. <br>3. Strong commitment to understanding how technology can impact the rights of women, racial and ethnic minorities, children, older people, people with disabilities, people living in poverty and low-wage workers, and other populations whose rights may be disproportionately impacted by AI is desirable.<br>4. Proven track record of producing timely and high-quality written research and investigations, as well as editing experience is required.<br>5. Ability to present and defend complex technology-related issues and positions to officials in governments, companies, and other bodies and institutions is preferable.<br>6. Being comfortable with generating and executing research projects, and the curiosity and creativity to follow through and follow up is required.<br>7. Exceptionally strong research, analytical, writing, and editing skills are required.<br>8. Experience conducting challenging investigative research globally is required, as is the ability to dig deep and tenacity in finding hard-to-get information, sources and records.<br>9. Good oral and written communication skills in English, and strong public speaking skills, are required; proficiency in other languages, is highly desirable.<br>10. Experience with TV, radio, print, and social media is highly desirable.<br>11. Demonstrated ability to work independently as well as successfully with a team and across other teams is required.<br>12. Strong interpersonal skills to work collaboratively within HRW, as well as develop constructive relationships with NGO partners, and company and government officials are required.<br>13. Demonstrated awareness and sensitivity to the needs and concerns of individuals from diverse cultures, backgrounds, and orientations is required.</p> <p><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>Salary and Benefits</strong></span>: HRW offers competitive compensation and employer-paid benefits. HRW offers relocation assistance package and will assist employees in obtaining necessary work authorization in all listed locations except Nairobi, if required; citizens of all nationalities are encouraged to apply. If based in the United States, the salary range would be 88,000 – 104,000. Salary ranges outside of the United States vary based on location.<br> <br><span style="text-decoration: underline;"><strong>How to Apply</strong></span>: Please apply by December 13, 2026, by visiting our online job portal at careers.hrw.org and submitting a cover letter and CV or resume. No calls or email inquiries, please. Only complete applications will be reviewed and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. <br> <br>If you are experiencing technical difficulties with your application submission, or if you require disability-related accommodation, please email ----- Rights Watch is strong because it is diverse</strong>. We actively seek a diverse applicant pool and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Human Rights Watch does not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, or criminal record. We welcome all kinds of diversity. Our employees include people who are parents and nonparents, the self-taught and university educated, and from a wide span of socio-economic backgrounds and perspectives on the world. Human Rights Watch is an equal opportunity employer. </em><br><em> </em><br><em><strong>Human Rights Watch </strong>is an international human rights monitoring and advocacy organization known for its in-depth investigations, its incisive and timely reporting, its innovative and high-profile advocacy campaigns, and its success in changing the human rights-related policies and practices of influential governments and international institutions. </em></p> Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Customer Success Leader, Enterprise Law Firms, Northern Europe
description: Why Harvey At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come. This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. Role Overview As Customer Success Leader, you lead the team that is custodian of value for Harvey's Enterprise law-firm customers across Northern Europe. You own gross and net revenue retention across the segment, built on Harvey becoming embedded in how each firm's practice groups work and every firm moving along the AI maturity curve. You will be a visible executive presence with managing partners and firm leadership across a portfolio of prestigious, high-profile firms. As a member of the broader Customer Success leadership team, you will set the strategy, playbooks and operating rhythm that let every CSM run their book as a portfolio and deliver a consistently high standard for every firm. Through empathetic leadership and a high bar, you will hire and develop CSMs into trusted advisers to innovation leaders, practice group leaders and managing partners, so partners and associates see undeniable value and each firm builds a lasting AI advantage. You will also partner across Harvey's go-to-market, product and legal engineering teams to shape how we serve law firms end to end. What You'll Do Build and lead a high-performing team : hire, coach and develop Enterprise Law Firm CSMs across Northern Europe, promoting a culture of accountability, execution, growth and relentless improvement. Own retention, expansion and renewal readiness : run the segment as a portfolio — knowing, with evidence, whether each firm needs protecting or growing — surface risk early, build expansion plans with Sales where there is room to grow, ensure every firm is multi-threaded, and forecast accurately against gross and net revenue retention targets. Prove value : coach your team to align each firm on measurable outcomes — capacity, realisation, matter economics, client impact — and capture the value stories and ROI evidence that underpin renewal and growth. Lead at partner level : grow CSMs into trusted advisers who cultivate champions and partner sponsors, and engage directly with managing partners, senior partners and innovation leaders at the segment's key firms. Set the standard for the firm's journey : define and scale the playbooks — mutual success plans tied to each firm's objectives, kickoffs, implementation reviews, QBRs and executive business reviews — that take every firm from pilot to daily use, practice group by practice group. Orchestrate cross-functionally : partner with Sales, Legal Engineering, Innovation Partners, the Transformation Office and Product leaders so each firm gets the right expertise at the right moment. Run the product feedback flywheel : turn the voice of law-firm customers into prioritised input for Product and Engineering, and into improvements in how we deliver. What You Have Ideal candidates for the Customer Success Leader, Enterprise Law Firms role at Harvey can demonstrate comfort and experience with the following: A proven background leading high-performing Customer Success or account management teams in late-stage or post-IPO enterprise SaaS, serving strategic or lighthouse accounts with substantial six-figure annual spend — ideally law firms or other professional services firms. A track record of owning and delivering a team-level revenue, retention or net-revenue-retention number, with accurate forecasting. Building teams through hiring, coaching and developing talent, with a leadership style grounded in empathy and a high bar. Designing and scaling playbooks that take enterprise customers from initial adoption to embedded, organisation-wide use, with measurable outcomes grounded in concrete use cases. Building multi-threaded relationships at senior level and influencing partners and stakeholders who did not buy the product. Portfolio planning and revenue-based prioritisation across a regional book, including early identification and mitigation of risk. Quantifying and communicating business value and ROI to senior legal stakeholders. An AI-native way of working: you use AI and sophisticated tooling daily, can show how it has changed your own and your team's output, and have a point of view on how AI changes legal practice. Communicating and influencing at every level, internally and externally, including running in-person meetings with managing partners and firm leadership. Law-firm experience is a strong plus: an understanding of how partnerships make decisions, how practice groups differ and what partners, associates and innovation teams each care about, ideally in the Northern European legal market. Adapting seamlessly in the face of high-speed change and growth, with a strong point of view and proactive self-management. Depending on your location, an Applicant Privacy Notice may apply to you. title: Senior Social Media Manager - UK
description: Developers decide what’s interesting long before they decide what to buy. They follow builders, share the talk everyone is watching, and argue about benchmarks in the replies. Most infrastructure brands show up in that feed looking and sounding the same. ClickHouse has the material to do something different: a fast, open-source database that has grown into a platform for real-time analytics, data warehousing, observability, and AI workloads; engineers and leaders with real points of view; and a brand that already turns up in unexpected places, from a Premier League partnership to our own Open House conference. We are looking for a Senior Social Media Manager to run the ClickHouse accounts and turn that material into a brand developers actually want to follow, at the intersection of infrastructure, technology, and culture. You’ll own our presence on LinkedIn, X, and YouTube with video at the center: clipping talks, podcasts, launches, and live moments into content that travels, building formats people come back for, and working with the creators developers already trust. You’ll be accountable for growing audience and engagement across a global community. You’ll sit on the Story & Communications team, reporting to the Head of Story & Communications, and work closely with developer relations, product marketing, demand generation, events, and our brand and design team. This is a hands-on role: you’ll make the work, not only schedule it. What You Will Be Doing Run the ClickHouse accounts on LinkedIn, X, and YouTube end to end: strategy, voice, calendar, publishing, and community management, with an approach built for each channel and for a global audience across time zones Put video at the center of how ClickHouse shows up: clip talks, podcasts, livestreams, launches, and executive moments into short-form and vertical content, and build recurring, social-first series that earn a following Build a brand developers find interesting at the intersection of infrastructure, technology, and culture, pairing technical depth with humor, working and why Track what developers say about ClickHouse and the category and feed it back to product marketing, developer relations, and campaign teams, while using AI tooling and a lean production workflow to ship content quickly and partnering with demand generation so the best organic work gets paid reach What You Bring Along A record of growing audience and engagement at scale for a brand title: Biomedical Scientist
description: Mission Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne. In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave. As a team, we chase 10X, not 10%, and we’re looking for people who think the same way to help us scale what we’ve started in Sweden, the UK, and now the US. Join the clinicians, engineers and business builders making prevention a routine part of care. Role Purpose This is not a traditional laboratory role. We're looking for a Biomedical Scientist who is comfortable working differently, embraces innovation, and takes pride in delivering accurate results at exceptional pace. Neko Health members come through our clinics for whole-body preventive health screenings, and our laboratories sit at the centre of the patient journey. They are busy, modern spaces, and the service continues to develop as we scale. This is a hands-on, autonomous role, based on site in one of our central London laboratories. As a Biomedical Scientist, you will operate our Abbott Alinity and Sysmex XN-550 analysers and support the quality systems that allow us to return results within 30 minutes of sample receipt. If you're a BMS looking to further develop your career in an innovation-led environment, we would love to hear from you. What You'll Deliver in the First 6 - 12 Months Initialise the analysers each day and ready them for sample processing. Perform testing on our Abbott Alinity (biochemistry and immunoassay) and Sysmex XN-550 (haematology) analysers, validating patient results and escalating clinically anomalous or unexpected findings. Carry out daily calibration, internal quality control, and routine maintenance of analysers, troubleshooting and escalating technical issues promptly. Work within our ISO 15189-aligned, UKAS-facing quality management system: author SOP updates, monitor EQA performance, support audits, and investigate non-conformances. Contribute to service improvement work, including analyser verification, reagent evaluation, and software testing. Maintain accurate, auditable records and support performance monitoring across turnaround times, KPIs, and consumables usage. Provide technical guidance to clinical colleagues and support training across the lab team. Minimum Requirements HCPC registration as a Biomedical Scientist, with evidence of ongoing CPD. Minimum one year of post-registration experience in clinical chemistry and immunoassay, including IQC and EQA practice. Demonstrable experience operating an integrated clinical chemistry and immunoassay analyser. Experience working accurately and efficiently under time pressure, suited to a low-volume, fast-turnaround service model. Preferred Post-registration experience in haematology. Hands-on experience operating Sysmex XN-series haematology analysers. Hands-on experience operating Abbott Alinity ci-series. Experience in POCT, rapid diagnostics, or high-throughput clinical settings. Experience with laboratory information management systems (LIMS), digital result reporting, or involvement in LIMS development and user acceptance testing. title: Area Medical Lead, North & Midlands
description: Mission Neko Health is a health technology company that opened its first clinic in Stockholm in 2018, founded by Daniel Ek and Hjalmar Nilsonne. In one hour, our scan combines radiation-free imaging, heart and circulation measurements, and same-visit blood results with time to talk it through with a clinician, so people can act on what matters before symptoms appear. We design and build our own hardware, software and clinical protocols, and more than 100,000 members have already had a scan, with 75% booking and prepaying their next one before they leave. That means every consultation in your area meets the same threshold of safety, quality, and member experience across your region. It means the clinical teams working with you are developing, not just performing. It means clinical issues are being seen and addressed before they show up in audits or member complaints. And it means the quality metrics for your region are known, owned and moving in the right direction. And it means clinical judgment shows up at the table when operational decisions are being made. You'll partner closely with the UK Medical Director, who holds final clinical authority for the UK market, and operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager for your region who owns the operational side. The clinical health of the region is yours. Ensure lead clinicians in your market(s) are performing excellently and that the clinical teams have the appropriate clinical escalation pathways in place. Support clinical hiring for your area against defined criteria, and partner with the Training and Education team to close training gaps as they emerge. Own the review and closure of clinical incidents and near-misses in your area, making sure learnings are actually applied, not just documented. Own the quality metrics for your region: accountable for performance against Neko's medical quality goals at area level, including scan quality (perfect scan score), member follow-up quality and timeliness (perfect follow-up score and follow-up SLAs), clinical safety (Northstar Clinical Safety score) and clinician summary quality and timeliness. Review the data with your Area Clinic Manager each week and month, trace variation to root cause by site and clinician, set improvement actions, and report progress and risks to the UK Medical Director. Operate in true dyad partnership with the Area Clinic Manager: co-owning quality, member experience, and business goals, attending and contributing to Weekly and Monthly Business Reviews, and bringing clinical input into operational decisions before they're made. Round your sites regularly to observe, support, and listen, surfacing what's working so it can spread, and what isn't so it can be addressed. Build and maintain trusted relationships with the GPs, NHS trusts and private specialist clinicians who receive Neko referrals, monitoring referral quality and addressing breakdowns quickly. Know the UK regulatory landscape: CQC registration and inspection standards, GMC/NMC professional standards and revalidation, NHS and GP referral pathways and obligations, and UK-specific clinical rules, and flag emerging risks before they become problems. Lead or participate in clinical pilots as required - defining success, capturing learnings, and documenting outcomes so the rest of the company can learn from your region. What We're Hiring For Holds the Bar at Scale. You're the kind of clinical leader who can make sure every consultation feels the same regardless of site or clinician, not by micromanaging, but by setting a clear standard, coaching to it, and noticing when it drifts. You're rigorous without being rigid. Develops the Clinicians You Lead. You take clinician development seriously. You give honest feedback even when it's uncomfortable. You spot what someone needs before they ask. You know the difference between a clinician who needs coaching and one who needs to leave, and you don't avoid either conversation. The Dyad That Actually Works. You bring clinical judgment into operational decisions before they're made and you stay constructive when clinical standards and operational targets pull in different directions. When you escalate, it's because something genuinely needs leadership attention, not because you've stopped trying to resolve it locally. Reads the Pattern, Not Just the Report. You don't just review the data. You see what it's telling you. You round your sites and notice things that don't show up in dashboards. When you spot a pattern you trace it to the root cause and you make sure the right people hear about it. Trusted Outside the Walls. The referral network, the regulators, the specialist clinicians who receive Neko members: these relationships sit with you. You represent Neko credibly because you're a credible clinician yourself. People in the local medical community know your name, and when you flag something, they take it seriously. Minimum Requirements Full GMC registration with a license to practice, in good standing and with a current revalidation, and right to work in the UK. On the GMC GP Register with qualification (CCT or equivalent) in General Practice. 4+ years of medical leadership experience in the UK health system (NHS and/or private sector), including direct management of clinicians. Demonstrated experience holding clinical standards across multiple sites or a large clinical team. Preferred Experience in preventive care, tech enabled healthcare or longitudinal care models. Experience operating in a clinical-operational dyad structure. Experience leading clinical pilots or scaling new clinical workflows across multiple sites. We don't just work in the sporting industry; we are actively changing it. All of which will have a direct impact on customers and their experiences with the product. This role suits a strong generalist who has seen many parts of engineering. You might have worked on any of the following: high-throughput systems, computer vision, robotics, ML infrastructure, or other complex applications. Our ideal candidate brings strong engineering judgment, good technical range, and the ability to learn quickly. You will be hands-on, working in Python and C++ on devices and services in use by our customers every day. WHAT YOU'LL DO Design and implement algorithms for 3D object tracking, segmentation, and motion recognition on embedded hardware. Train and iterate on ML models — from dataset curation through training, evaluation, and deployment to edge devices. Help bring ML, computer vision, or signal-processing systems into production with tight performance constraints Build reliable application features and services that customers use in real environments. Analyze production data to find system limits, product issues, and opportunities for improvement. Collaborate closely with the embedded platform team on model optimization and inference performance, and with the applications team on how tracking data becomes product features. WHAT YOU'LL NEED 4+ years of software engineering experience in production systems. Strong skill in Python and backend engineering. Working knowledge of C++ or a strong reason to be effective in performance-critical code. Experience with data-intensive systems, distributed systems, parallel processing, or efficient data pipelines. Exposure to ML, ML infrastructure, signal processing, real-time systems, computer vision, or related applied technical areas. A track record of shipping reliable software, not only prototypes. Strong debugging skills and the ability to find the root cause of complex system behavior. Clear communication and good judgment when tradeoffs are not simple. Curiosity, adaptability, and the desire to learn new technical areas. Nice to have — and what would make you exceptional: Experience with computer vision, depth cameras, pose estimation, tracking, or 3D data. Experience with ML model deployment, feature pipelines, evaluation systems, or data quality tools. Experience with streaming data, event systems, real-time processing, or low-latency applications. Experience with numerical methods, signal processing, filtering, state estimation, or robotics. You'll also build ClickZ's network of event partners, contributors, PR contacts and industry leaders, and meet many of them in person at industry events.</p> <p>You'll work closely with ClickZ's lead, who sets the brand's strategy, and you'll have real ownership of your workstreams from the start. This is an <strong>office-based role</strong> in London.</p> <p>This role suits someone with a journalist's instinct for a story, a marketer's eye for an audience, and the energy to keep both going every week.</p> <h2> </h2> <h2>What you'll work on</h2> <p>Your time will be spread across three areas, with content creation at the core. All three serve one goal: growing the ClickZ brand and getting its content to more of the right people.</p> <table> <thead> <tr> <th>Focus area</th> <th>What it covers</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody> <tr> <td>Content creation</td> <td>The core of the role: editorial content on market trends, event coverage, brand leadership interviews and Q&As, flagship newsletters, and social content</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Audience growth and content analysis</td> <td>Growing ClickZ's readership and subscribers, testing new formats, and using performance data to decide what to create next</td> </tr> <tr> <td>Network and community</td> <td>Building relationships with event partners, marketing and commerce leaders, PR teams and contributors, online and in person at industry events</td> </tr> </tbody> </table> <h2> </h2> <h2>Key Responsibilities</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Keep the content engine fed.</strong> Track the news and trends that matter to marketing and commerce leaders, and turn them into timely, well-argued content.</li> <li><strong>Raise the bar on every channel.</strong> Bring a creative eye to email, social and web content, and build a distinct content plan for each channel.</li> <li><strong>Shape the flagship newsletters.</strong> Draft and refine ClickZ's flagship newsletters, and develop more tailored formats for different parts of the audience.</li> <li><strong>Bring leadership conversations to life.</strong> Prepare and support podcast and Q&A conversations with leaders across marketing and commerce, and, with training and support, grow into hosting them.</li> <li><strong>Grow the audience.</strong> Work out which formats and topics readers respond to, and turn readers into subscribers. You should apply if you meet these six must-haves:</p> <ul> <li>Have around one year of experience creating content in the digital marketing, media or commerce world, whether in journalism, editorial, content or social roles (internships, placements and personal projects count), and a genuine passion for digital marketing and commerce, and for the leaders shaping them</li> <li>Have <strong>strong editorial judgement</strong>: you can tell good content from weak, and relevant from noise, and you know a big story when you see one (experience of writing, editing or curating, including student or personal publications)</li> <li>Bring a <strong>creative eye to content</strong> across email, social and web, with a feel for multimedia formats</li> <li>Are <strong>audience-minded</strong>: you think about who's reading, how to reach more of the right people and how to build a community around a brand. You're also comfortable with data: you use performance numbers to make content decisions and back up your conclusions (experience using analytics such as GA4)</li> <li>Are <strong>agentically minded</strong>: you love experimenting with new tools for multimedia content creation and adaptation, and know when to push them and when to take over</li> <li>Are <strong>a natural conversationalist</strong>: you get a guest talking, hold your own with senior leaders, and leave an event with new connections</li> </ul> <p><strong>Also important:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Have <strong>high agency</strong>: you take ownership of your work, stretch beyond the brief and challenge the status quo when something could be better</li> <li>Enjoy a fast-paced, innovative startup environment, where you'll ship quickly, iterate often and juggle several projects at once</li> <li>Are happy to travel for industry events, within the UK and occasionally overseas</li> </ul> workplace pension, through Royal London, with Fospha matching your contributions up to 3%</li> <li>A £1,000/year flexible benefits allowance to put towards private medical insurance, dental cover, a annual salary, from day one</li> <li>Cycle to Work scheme, plus discounts on everyday spending through our benefits portal — Apple, Tesco, IKEA, M&S, Deliveroo, cinema tickets and more</li> snacks, and Lunch & Learn events at our Scale Space office, plus access to the wider Blenheim Chalcot community</li&g

title: Commercial Customer Success Manager
description: A little about us incident.io is the AI software reliability platform trusted by engineering teams at Notion, Linear, Ramp and 2,000+ companies who can't afford downtime. The stakes are real, the talent is insane, and somehow it's a genuinely lovely place to work. We all pull our weight, go the extra mile, and put in the bit of magic most companies don't have time for, all while having fun and never taking ourselves too seriously. We've raised $100+ million from Index Ventures, Insight Partners, and Point Nine, and we're growing fast. There's never been a better time to join. The role in one line Customers trust us when things go wrong. We're the software reliability platform built to investigate, respond to and prevent incidents. As a Commercial CSM, you're the partner to our mid-market engineering teams - getting them onboarded, embedded and expanding their usage, and maturing their incident management and reliability as they grow. What that looks like day to day Our Customer Success organisation is at the heart of incident.io . We're the team closest to our customers' hardest problems, and we're trusted to solve them. We believe in a customer-led product approach, working hand in hand with Product to uncover and address what each customer really needs. Our goal goes beyond satisfaction: we want to delight customers at every stage of their journey, and build long-term relationships grounded in trust, shared success and mutual growth. You'll look after 70–80 Commercial customers: growth-oriented tech companies, mostly under 1,000 people, between $30k and $150k ARR each. Industry leaders like Vanta, Monday.com and Loom sit in this segment. Some are steady, some are scaling fast, and much of the job is knowing which is which, and what each one needs from you. Most of your time goes to mid-market customers on our top-tier plan, where you're their dedicated CSM leading onboarding and adoption. You'll blend 1:1 time with scalable programmes to get teams to value quickly: best-practice sessions, end-user training, partnership and roadmap reviews. You'll also cover a subset of smaller customers in a low-touch capacity, leaning on usage data to spot risk and opportunity early. Day to day, this is a high ownership role. You'll help customers navigate the product, unpick problems when they hit them, and keep everyone pointed at the outcomes their team actually cares about. You are responsible for proactively identifying expansion and upsell opportunities, and partnering with Sales and Expansion Account Managers to grow revenue within your accounts. Internally, you're the voice of the Commercial customer with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing and Support. There's still a lot to build and a ton of opportunity for you to shape this segment. The Commercial motion works, but scaling and automating the customer journey is live work we're ramping up now - refining playbooks, automating the repeatable stuff, building the tooling and content that makes a portfolio this size easier to serve. We're AI-forward in how we approach it, so you'd be shaping this rather than inheriting it. Who you are You've carried a book of 40 to 100+ accounts and worked out how to be present across all of them without going quiet on half. You've sold to, or supported, technical people, whether that's engineering teams, on-call rotations or developer tools. You can hold your own in a technical conversation without needing to escalate every one of them. You've got commercial instincts. You spot the account that's about to double, you know what a growth signal looks like, and you know how to steer a renewal to a good outcome. You know what scaled CS looks like when it's done well. Playbooks, one-to-many programs, AI-assisted workflows. You don't need to have built them from scratch, but you've worked around them enough to have opinions on what you'd do differently. Half-built process doesn't rattle you. You'd rather fix the documentation than complain about it. You actually like being in a room with customers, and you'll get on a plane for the right one. Supporting you We work hard and we think life outside work matters just as much. Our benefits pack is built to support both. Private medical insurance. Seriously good cover — we want you and the people you love to be looked after. Competitive annual leave. Showing up at your best requires switching off, and we make sure you have time to do that. First Friday of every month off. Yes, seriously. Enhanced pension. We put real money in, because future-you deserves better than an afterthought. Meaningful equity. We're rapidly scaling, and everyone who helps shape the outcome should share in it. Unlimited AI spend. For everyone, not just engineers. We're all-in on AI across the company, and we expect you to be too. Generous parental leave. The early days with a new baby matter more than anything we're doing here, and we want you to be present for them. Two budgets that have your back. £1000 to invest in your setup, £500 a year to invest in yourself. Compensation: £85K – £118K • Offers Equity London • £85K – £118K • Offers Equity Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

description: Senior Data Protection Engineer (Backup & Cyber Resilience) Location: Windsor, UK Introduction We’re hiring a S enior Data Protection Engineer to join a global hosting and managed services team . The team runs business-critical, highly regulated systems for organisations around the world, many of them in healthcare, where losing data or failing to recover it is not an option. This is a senior role with real influence. You’ll own the enterprise backup and recovery platform across all regions. You’ll set the standards for how data is protected, retained and restored, and you’ll show, with evidence, that recovery targets are met. You’ll also help shape where data protection services go next, at a time when cyber resilience matters more than ever. Responsibilities & Tasks Run the platform globally. Lead the engineering, administration and continuous improvement of an enterprise Rubrik environment. This covers configuration, upgrades, capacity planning, health monitoring, security hardening and lifecycle management. Set the rules. Design and enforce global protection policies, including SLA tiers, retention, archiving, replication, immutability, encryption and access controls. Turn requirements into protection. Convert business, regulatory, contractual and risk needs into clear protection tiers, RPO and RTO targets, and practical operating procedures. Keep coverage complete. Bring new workloads into the service and keep protection accurate across on-premises, cloud, virtualised, database and application environments. Keep operations healthy. Monitor backup, replication, archiving and restore activity. Fix failed jobs, capacity pressure, performance issues and policy exceptions before they become risks. Prove that recovery works. Plan and run restore tests, disaster recovery exercises and readiness reviews, and keep the evidence that recovery targets and controls are met. Strengthen cyber resilience. Work with security and incident response teams on ransomware readiness, anomaly investigations, clean-recovery planning and privileged-access controls. Build strong governance. Write the runbooks, standards and procedures that define good practice, and help regions and technology teams adopt them consistently. Lead when it counts. Take technical ownership during incidents and service disruptions, and drive root cause analysis and lasting corrective actions. Automate. Use APIs, scripting and orchestration tools to automate routine operations, compliance checks, reporting and workflows. Report clearly. Give regular insight into protection coverage, recoverability, compliance, capacity, platform risk and operational performance. Work across teams. Partner closely with infrastructure, cloud, database, application, security, risk and business continuity colleagues, and take part in a shared on-call rota for critical production services. Requirements & Qualifications Essential: A solid track record of engineering and running enterprise-scale backup, recovery and data protection services Extensive hands-on production experience with Rubrik A current Rubrik Certified System Administrator (RCSA) certification Experience designing and rolling out data protection policies, standards and operating models across multiple regions A strong grasp of retention, immutability, encryption, access control, RPO and RTO, and recovery validation Hands-on involvement in disaster recovery, cyber recovery or ransomware-resilience initiatives Strong troubleshooting skills, and familiarity with incident, change and problem management processes Experience supporting production services in a 24x7 or on-call environment Benefits & Culture Global reach and visible impact: Your work will directly protect critical services, including healthcare systems that clinicians and care providers rely on every day. Real ownership: You’ll have a strong voice in policy design, retention strategy, cyber resilience, automation and the long-term direction of the service. Collaborative environment: You’ll join experienced engineers and architects who value shared ownership, operational excellence and openly sharing knowledge. Growth and development: You’ll keep developing your skills on an enterprise-grade platform, with support for certifications and continuous learning. Competitive rewards: The package includes market-aligned pay and comprehensive benefits that reflect a senior technical role. If you want to make data protection dependable at a global scale, we’d love to hear from you. Find Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
description: <p>We are hiring a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to contribute to cutting-edge Research & Development. As innovators in speech technology, our mission is to Understand Every Voice - a vision that has propelled us to be world leaders of Voice AI. Fuelled by innovation, inclusivity, and a passion for making a global impact through world-leading Speech AI, we're looking for an experienced Senior Machine Learning Engineer to accelerate our efforts towards exceptional speech solutions.</p> <p>Our Modelling Team trains diverse models, including large self-supervised ones, supporting Speechmatics towards being the most accurate speech recognition system globally. It also ensures their deployment into production, working with the latest developments in ML, but also with the best engineering practices for software engineering and model serving.</p> <p><strong>What you’ll be doing:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Work on complex R&D projects, with a diverse group of engineers, to achieve ambitious goals.</li> <li>Stay current with the latest developments in Machine learning.</li> <li>Execute high-impact projects to ensure team success.</li> <li>Work collaboratively across departments and mentor team members (where appropriate).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Who we are looking for:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Demonstrated experience in collaboratively pursuing ambitious R&D agendas.</li> <li>Precise attention to detail, but is also aware of how the big picture relates to company goals, and where the field of Machine Learning is headed towards.</li> <li>Understanding of the modern Machine Learning stack, for example:<br>- Knowledge of contemporary transformer architectures (e.g., GQA, KV-caching) and best practices.<br>- Experience in distributed training techniques.<br>- Familiarity with optimisation strategies for model inference (e.g., dynamic batching, flash attention, speculative decoding).</li> <li>With preferred backgrounds covering <span style="text-decoration: underline;">some</span> of the following:<br>- Publications in top-tier conferences.<br>- Contributions to popular open-source repositories.<br>- Technical writing skills as evidenced by relevant publications or blogs.</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><em><span class="ui-provider a b c d e f g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z ab ac ae af ag ah ai aj ak">We encourage you to apply even if you do not feel you match all of the requirements exactly. The list of requirements is intended to show the kinds of experience and qualities we’re looking for, but it is not exhaustive. If you are interested in the role, the team, and our mission, we would love to consider your application. We are always open to conversations and look forward to hearing from you.</span></em></p> <p><strong>Who we are:</strong></p> <p class="p1">Speechmatics is the leading expert in Speech Intelligence, and uses AI and Machine Learning to unlock business value in human speech worldwide. We work with an amazing mix of global companies, and our technology can integrate into our customers stack irrespective of their industry or use case – making it the go-to solution to harness useful information from speech.</p> <p class="p1">Joining us means working with some of the smartest minds around the world, focused on cutting-edge projects and deploying the latest techniques to disrupt the market. We believe in putting people first; we’ll do all we can to help you develop your skills and give you the tools you need to thrive. Our Focus Fridays give you an undisturbed day of focus, offset with Together Tuesdays when we have our team meetings, so you've always got the right balance.</p> <p class="p1">We have structured a hybrid approach that includes 2-3 designated office days each week. This arrangement ensures that while we embrace the advantages of remote work, we also maintain the vital connection and synergy that only in-person interactions can foster.</p> <p class="p1">This is only the beginning; we’re looking for amazing people like you to continue our journey…</p> <p class="p1"><strong>What we can offer you:<br></strong></p> <p class="p1">No matter what stage of your career you’re at - from paid internships and first-job opportunities through to management and senior positions - we’ll support you with the training and development needed to reach your career aspirations with us. There really is no shortage of opportunities here for you to get involved and collaborate with those around you to deliver your best work.</p> <p class="p1">We offer incredibly flexible working, regular company lunches, and birthday celebrations. But that’s not all. We’ve spoken to our teams to find out what they want. From Private Medical, and Dental for you and your family, through to global working opportunities, a generous holiday allowance and pension/401K matching, we want to make sure our employees and their families are looked after. Every employee will receive a working from home allowance for tech or home office equipment (on top of your choice of laptop and accessories of course). Our approach to parental leave is designed to support employees globally. While this varies by geo, we have support in place for parents (including adoption assistance and reproductive health services) to ensure they have the time and financial resources needed to care for their growing families.</p> <p><strong>At Speechmatics, our mission is simple: Understand Every Voice out there.</strong> </p> <p>That's not just about our tech – it's the heart and soul of who we are. We welcome different experiences, viewpoints, and identities. For us, it’s not just the right thing to do; it’s our catalyst for sparking innovation and creativity.
